sentences.zh: 陶琰，字廷信，絳州人。

translations.literal: Tao Yan, styled Tingxin, was a man of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Yan, styled Tingxin, was a native of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 父銓，進士，陜西右參議。

translations.literal: His father Quan was a jinshi and Right Assistant Administration Commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Quan was a jinshi and served as Right Assistant Administration Commissioner of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 琰舉成化七年鄉試第一，十七年成進士，授刑部主事。

translations.literal: Yan placed first in the provincial examination in the seventh year of Chenghua; in the seventeenth year he became a jinshi and was appointed a principal secretary in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Yan ranked first in the provincial examination of Chenghua 7, passed the jinshi examination in Chenghua 17, and was appointed a principal secretary in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 弘治初，進員外郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Hongzhi he was advanced to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Hongzhi reign he was promoted to vice director.

sentences.zh: 歷固原兵備副使。

translations.literal: He served successively as Assistant Surveillance Commissioner for military defense at Guyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as the Guyuan military-defense assistant surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 練士卒，廣芻粟。

translations.literal: He drilled soldiers and expanded fodder and grain stores.
translations.idiomatic: He drilled the troops and expanded stores of fodder and grain.

sentences.zh: 歷九年，部內晏如。

translations.literal: After nine years the area under his charge was peaceful and secure.
translations.idiomatic: After nine years the region under his jurisdiction was calm and secure.

sentences.zh: 遷福建按察使，浙江左布政使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Fujian as surveillance commissioner and to Zhejiang as left administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Fujian as surveillance commissioner and to Zhejiang as left administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 正德初，以右副都御史巡撫河南，遷刑部右侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengde he was made right censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Henan, then transferred to right vice minister of punishments.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhengde reign he was appointed Right Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Henan, then promoted to Right Vice Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 陜西遊擊徐謙訐御史李高。

translations.literal: Xu Qian, a mobile detachment commander in Shaanxi, accused the censor Li Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Qian, a mobile-detachment commander in Shaanxi, accused the censor Li Gao.

sentences.zh: 謙故劉瑾黨，行厚賂，欲中高危法。

translations.literal: Qian was formerly of Liu Jin's faction; he offered heavy bribes and sought to trap Gao in a capital offense.
translations.idiomatic: Qian had been a partisan of Liu Jin; he offered heavy bribes and sought to entrap Gao in a capital crime.

sentences.zh: 琰往按，直高。

translations.literal: Yan went to investigate and found Gao innocent.
translations.idiomatic: Yan went to investigate and cleared Gao.

sentences.zh: 瑾怒，假他事下琰詔獄，褫其職，又罰米四百石輸邊。

translations.literal: Jin was enraged; on a pretext he had Yan thrown into the imperial prison, stripped of office, and fined four hundred piculs of grain for delivery to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was furious; on another charge he had Yan thrown into the imperial prison, stripped of his post, and fined four hundred piculs of grain for the frontier.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，起左副都御史，總督漕運兼巡撫準、揚諸府。

translations.literal: When Jin was executed, Yan was restored as left censor-in-chief, placed in general charge of grain transport, and made grand coordinator of Huaiyang and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin was executed, Yan was recalled as Left Censor-in-Chief, placed in overall charge of grain transport on the Grand Canal, and made Grand Coordinator of Huai, Yang, and the other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 六年，轉南京刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to vice minister of punishments at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was transferred to Vice Minister of Punishments at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 明年，賊劉七等將犯江南，王浩八又入衢州。

translations.literal: The next year the bandits Liu Qi and others were about to invade Jiangnan, and Wang Haoba again entered Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the bandits Liu Qi and his fellows were about to raid Jiangnan, and Wang Haoba again entered Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 進琰右都御史，巡視浙江。

translations.literal: Yan was advanced to right censor-in-chief and sent to inspect Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief and sent to inspect Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 至則七等已滅，浩八聽撫。

translations.literal: When he arrived, Liu Qi and his fellows had already been destroyed and Haoba had submitted to pacification.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he arrived, Liu Qi and his band had already been wiped out and Haoba had accepted pacification.

sentences.zh: 會寧、紹瀕海地颶風大作，居民漂沒萬數。

translations.literal: Just then a hurricane struck the coastal regions of Hui and Shao, and tens of thousands of inhabitants were swept away.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time a typhoon struck the coastal districts of Hui and Shao, and tens of thousands of residents were swept away in the flood.

sentences.zh: 琰出帑金振救，而大築蕭山至會稽堤五萬余丈。

translations.literal: Yan disbursed treasury funds for relief and built dikes of more than fifty thousand zhang from Xiaoshan to Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Yan drew on treasury funds for relief and undertook a great dike project of more than fifty thousand zhang from Xiaoshan to Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 奏設兵備道守要害，防浩八黨出沒，遣將擊斬其渠魁。

translations.literal: He memorialized to establish a military-defense circuit to guard strategic points against Haoba's partisans, and sent generals to strike down their ringleaders.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to establish a military-defense circuit to hold the key points against Haoba's followers, and sent generals to attack and behead their leaders.

sentences.zh: 遂城開化、常山、遂安、蘭溪，境內以靖。

translations.literal: He then walled Kaihua, Changshan, Suian, and Lanxi, and the region within his jurisdiction was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He then fortified Kaihua, Changshan, Suian, and Lanxi, and the territory under his charge was brought to peace.

sentences.zh: 復命總督漕運，七疏乞歸。

translations.literal: He was again ordered to take general charge of grain transport and seven times memorialized to retire.
translations.idiomatic: He was again ordered to take overall charge of grain transport and memorialized seven times asking to retire.

sentences.zh: 世宗嗣位，起故官。

translations.literal: When the Shizong Emperor succeeded, he was recalled to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong succeeded to the throne, Yan was recalled to his former office.

sentences.zh: 凡三督漕，軍民習其政，不嚴而肅。

translations.literal: In all he directed grain transport three times; soldiers and civilians, accustomed to his administration, were orderly though he was not severe.
translations.idiomatic: In all he directed grain transport three times; soldiers and civilians, used to his ways, were orderly though he was not harsh.

sentences.zh: 琰性清儉，飯惟一疏。

translations.literal: Yan was by nature frugal and abstemious, taking only one simple dish at a meal.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was frugal by nature and took only a single simple dish at each meal.

sentences.zh: 每到官及罷去，行李止三竹笥。

translations.literal: Whenever he took up or left office, his baggage consisted of only three bamboo cases.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he arrived at or left a post, his luggage amounted to no more than three bamboo cases.

sentences.zh: 尋加戶部尚書。

translations.literal: Shortly he was given the additional title of minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was given the additional title of Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖元年召拜工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiajing he was summoned and appointed minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 1 he was summoned and appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 其冬，改南京兵部，加太子少保。

translations.literal: That winter he was transferred to the ministry of war at Nanjing and given the additional title of junior mentor to the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was transferred to the Ministry of War at Nanjing and given the additional title of Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 未浹歲，屢引年乞體。

translations.literal: Before a full year had passed he repeatedly cited his age and begged leave to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Before a full year had passed he repeatedly pleaded his age and asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 加太子太保，乘傳歸，有司歲時存問。

translations.literal: He was given the further title of grand mentor to the heir apparent and returned home with post-horses provided; local officials were ordered to inquire after him on holidays.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the further title of Grand Mentor to the Heir Apparent and returned home with relay horses; local officials were to call on him at the seasonal festivals.

sentences.zh: 又九年卒，年八十有四。

translations.literal: Nine years later he died, aged eighty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Nine years later he died, at the age of eighty-four.

sentences.zh: 贈少保，謚恭介。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as junior guardian and given the posthumous name Gongjie.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Junior Guardian and given the posthumous name Gongjie (Reverent and Incorruptible).

sentences.zh: 子滋，以進士授行人。

translations.literal: His son Zi, a jinshi, was appointed a courier-official.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zi, having passed the jinshi examination, was appointed a courier-official.

sentences.zh: 諫武宗南巡，杖闕下，謫國子學正。

translations.literal: He remonstrated against the Wuzong Emperor's southern tour, was beaten at the palace gate, and banished to be director of studies at the National University.
translations.idiomatic: He remonstrated against Emperor Wuzong's southern tour, was beaten at the palace gate, and was demoted to director of studies at the National University.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，歷兵部郎中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiajing he served as a director in the ministry of war.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jiajing reign he served as a director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 率同官伏闕爭「大禮」，再受杖，謫戍榆林。

translations.literal: Leading his colleagues he knelt at the gate to protest the "Grand Rites"; he was beaten a second time and exiled to garrison duty at Yulin.
translations.idiomatic: Leading his colleagues he knelt at the palace gate to protest the Grand Rites controversy; he was beaten again and exiled to military service at Yulin.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書王時中等言，琰老病呻吟，冀父子一相見，乞改調近衛。

translations.literal: The minister of war Wang Shizhong and others said that Yan, old and ill and groaning in pain, hoped only to see his son once more and begged that he be transferred to a nearer garrison.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of War Wang Shizhong and others said that Yan, old and ill and groaning in pain, hoped only that father and son might see each other once more, and asked that Zi be transferred to a nearer garrison.

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: The request was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 十五年赦還，卒。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was pardoned and returned, then died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was pardoned and returned home, then died.

sentences.zh: 王縝，字文哲，東莞人。

translations.literal: Wang Zhen, styled Wenzhe, was a man of Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen, styled Wenzhe, was a native of Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 父恪，寶慶知府。

translations.literal: His father Ke was prefect of Baqing.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ke was prefect of Baqing.

sentences.zh: 縝登弘治六年進士，選庶吉士，授兵科給事中。

translations.literal: Zhen passed the jinshi examination in the sixth year of Hongzhi, was chosen a Hanlin probationer, and appointed a supervising secretary in the bureau of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen passed the jinshi examination in Hongzhi 6, was selected as a Hanlin probationer, and was appointed a supervising secretary in the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 劾三邊總制王越附汪直、李廣，不可復玷節鉞。

translations.literal: He impeached Wang Yue, supreme commander of the three frontiers, for aligning with Wang Zhi and Li Guang, declaring that he should not again hold command authority.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Wang Yue, supreme commander of the three frontiers, for siding with Wang Zhi and Li Guang, declaring that he ought not again to hold military command.

sentences.zh: 出理南畿屯田。

translations.literal: He was sent out to administer military colonies in the southern capital region.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to administer military colonies in the southern metropolitan region.

sentences.zh: 有司征松江白絺六千匹，縝言絺非正供。

translations.literal: When local officials levied six thousand bolts of white silk gauze from Songjiang, Zhen said this gauze was not part of the regular tribute.
translations.idiomatic: When local officials levied six thousand bolts of white silk gauze from Songjiang, Zhen argued that such gauze was not part of the regular tribute.

sentences.zh: 且請停上清宮役。

translations.literal: He also requested suspension of labor on the Shangqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that labor on the Shangqing Palace be halted.

sentences.zh: 詔皆罷之。

translations.literal: An edict halted both measures.
translations.idiomatic: An edict halted both measures.

sentences.zh: 累遷工科都給事中。

translations.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to supervising secretary-in-chief of the bureau of works.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in succession to supervising secretary-in-chief of the Bureau of Works.

sentences.zh: 武宗初立，內府工匠以營造加恩。

translations.literal: When the Wuzong Emperor first ascended the throne, artisans of the inner palace were granted favors for construction work.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wuzong first took the throne, artisans of the inner palace were granted favors for construction work.

sentences.zh: 縝率同官言：「陛下初登大寶，工匠末技已有以微勞進者，誠不可示後世。

translations.literal: Zhen led his colleagues in saying: "Your Majesty has but lately ascended the great throne, and already craftsmen of trifling skill have been advanced for slight services—this truly cannot be shown to posterity.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen led his colleagues in saying, "Your Majesty has but lately ascended the great throne, and already artisans of trifling skill have been promoted for slight services—this truly cannot be shown to posterity.

sentences.zh: 宜散遣先朝諸畫士，革工匠所授官。」

translations.literal: You should dismiss the painters of the former reign and revoke the offices granted to artisans.
translations.idiomatic: You should dismiss the painters retained from the previous reign and revoke the offices granted to artisans.

sentences.zh: 帝不能用。

translations.literal: The emperor would not accept this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not accept this.

sentences.zh: 中官張永請改築通州新城，縝言泰陵工作方興，不當復興無益之役。

translations.literal: The eunuch Zhang Yong requested rebuilding the new city at Tongzhou; Zhen said work on the Tailing mausoleum had just begun and useless projects should not be revived.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Zhang Yong requested rebuilding the new city at Tongzhou; Zhen said work on the Tailing mausoleum had only just begun and that useless projects ought not be revived.

sentences.zh: 帝乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor then stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then halted the project.

sentences.zh: 正德元年出為山西右參政。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengde he went out as right assistant administration commissioner of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengde 1 he went out as Right Assistant Administration Commissioner of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 歷福建布政使，遷右副都御史，巡撫蘇、松諸府。

translations.literal: He served as administration commissioner of Fujian, then was made right censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Suzhou, Songjiang, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He served as administration commissioner of Fujian, then was appointed Right Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Suzhou, Songjiang, and the other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 協平江西賊王浩八。

translations.literal: He helped pacify the Jiangxi bandit Wang Haoba.
translations.idiomatic: He helped pacify the Jiangxi bandit Wang Haoba.

sentences.zh: 乾清宮災，疏請養宗室子宮中，定根本；

translations.literal: When the Qianqing Palace burned, he memorialized to rear a son of the imperial clan within the palace to secure the foundation;
translations.idiomatic: When the Qianqing Palace burned, he memorialized asking that a son of the imperial clan be reared within the palace to secure the succession;

sentences.zh: 去南京新增內官，召還建言被黜諸臣。

translations.literal: to dismiss the newly added inner eunuchs at Nanjing; and to recall the officials who had been dismissed for remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: to dismiss the newly added inner eunuchs at Nanjing; and to recall the officials who had been dismissed for offering remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No reply was received.
translations.idiomatic: No reply was received.

sentences.zh: 已，調鄖陽巡撫，遷南京刑部右侍郎。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred as grand coordinator of Yunyang and promoted to right vice minister of punishments at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was transferred as Grand Coordinator of Yunyang and promoted to Right Vice Minister of Punishments at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，陳正本十事。

translations.literal: When the Shizong Emperor ascended the throne, he set forth ten measures for restoring fundamental order.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong ascended the throne, he set forth ten measures for restoring fundamental order.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二年就擢戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiajing he was forthwith promoted to minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 2 he was forthwith promoted to Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 李充嗣，字士修，內江人。

translations.literal: Li Chongsi, styled Shixiu, was a man of Neijiang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chongsi, styled Shixiu, was a native of Neijiang.

sentences.zh: 給事中蕃孫也。

translations.literal: He was a grandson of the supervising secretary Fan.
translations.idiomatic: He was a grandson of the supervising secretary Fan.

sentences.zh: 登成化二十三年進士，改庶吉士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-third year of Chenghua and was transferred to be a Hanlin probationer.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Chenghua 23 and was transferred to be a Hanlin probationer.

sentences.zh: 弘治初，授戶部主事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Hongzhi he was appointed a principal secretary in the ministry of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Hongzhi reign he was appointed a principal secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 以從父臨安為郎中，改刑部。

translations.literal: Because his father's cousin Lin'an was a bureau director, he was transferred to the ministry of punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father's cousin Lin'an was a bureau director, he was transferred to the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 坐累，謫岳州通判。

translations.literal: He was implicated in a case and banished to be vice prefect of Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was implicated in a case and demoted to vice prefect of Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 久之，移隨州知州，擢陜西僉事，歷雲南按察使。

translations.literal: After a long while he was moved to be prefect of Suizhou, then promoted to assistant surveillance commissioner in Shaanxi and served as surveillance commissioner of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he was moved to prefect of Suizhou, then promoted to assistant surveillance commissioner in Shaanxi and served as surveillance commissioner of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 正德九年，舉治行卓異，累遷右副都御史，巡撫河南。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhengde, recognized for outstanding administration, he was promoted repeatedly to right censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengde 9, recognized for outstanding administration, he was promoted in succession to Right Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Henan.

sentences.zh: 歲大祲。

translations.literal: That year there was a great famine.
translations.idiomatic: That year there was a severe famine.

sentences.zh: 請發帑金移粟振之，不足，則勸貸富室。

translations.literal: He requested disbursement of treasury funds and transfer of grain for relief; when these were insufficient, he urged wealthy households to lend grain.
translations.idiomatic: He requested disbursement of treasury funds and transfer of grain for relief; when these proved insufficient, he urged wealthy households to lend grain.

sentences.zh: 時流民多聚開封，煮糜哺之。

translations.literal: At the time many refugees gathered at Kaifeng; he cooked gruel to feed them.
translations.idiomatic: At the time many refugees had gathered at Kaifeng; he cooked gruel to feed them.

sentences.zh: 逾月，資遣還鄉。

translations.literal: After more than a month he supplied funds to send them home.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month he provided funds to send them back to their home districts.

sentences.zh: 初，鎮守中官廖堂黨於劉瑾，假進貢名，要求百端，繼者以為常。

translations.literal: Earlier, the eunuch defender Liao Tang, a partisan of Liu Jin, had used the pretext of tribute to make demands of every kind; his successors took this as routine.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the eunuch defender Liao Tang, a partisan of Liu Jin, had used the pretext of tribute to make demands of every kind; his successors took this as routine.

sentences.zh: 充嗣言：「近中官進貢，有古銅器、窯變盆、黃鷹、角鷹、錦雞、走狗諸物，皆借名科斂。

translations.literal: Chongsi said: "Recently eunuchs presenting tribute have demanded antiquities in bronze, kiln-transformed basins, yellow hawks, horned hawks, brocaded fowl, hunting dogs, and the like—all levied under borrowed names.
translations.idiomatic: Chongsi said, "Recently, when eunuchs have presented tribute, they have demanded antiquities in bronze, kiln-transformed basins, yellow hawks, horned hawks, brocaded fowl, hunting dogs, and the like—all exacted under borrowed names.

sentences.zh: 外又有拜見銀、須知銀及侵扣驛傳快手月錢、河夫歇役之屬，無慮十余事，苛派動數十萬。

translations.literal: Besides these there are presentation silver, notification silver, and deductions from relay-post runners' monthly pay and boatmen's rest levies—no fewer than a dozen such items, with oppressive exactions often reaching hundreds of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond these there are presentation silver, notification silver, and deductions from relay-post runners' monthly pay and boatmen's rest levies—no fewer than a dozen such items, with oppressive levies often running into the hundreds of thousands.

sentences.zh: 其左右用事者，又私於境內抑買雜物，擅榷商賈貨利。

translations.literal: Their attendants in power further privately forced purchases of miscellaneous goods within the jurisdiction and monopolized merchants' profits.
translations.idiomatic: Their attendants in power further privately forced purchases of miscellaneous goods within the jurisdiction and arrogated merchants' profits to themselves.

sentences.zh: 乞嚴行禁絕。」

translations.literal: He begged that these be strictly forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that such practices be strictly forbidden.

sentences.zh: 詔但禁下人科取而已。

translations.literal: An edict forbade only the levies of subordinates under borrowed names.
translations.idiomatic: An edict went out forbidding only the exactions of subordinates under borrowed names.

sentences.zh: 十二年移撫應天諸府。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was transferred as grand coordinator of Yingtian and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was transferred as Grand Coordinator of Yingtian and the other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 寧王宸濠反，充嗣謂尚書喬宇曰：「都城守禦屬於公，畿輔則充嗣任之。」

translations.literal: When the Prince of Ning, Chen Hao, rebelled, Chongsi said to the minister Qiao Yu: "Defense of the capital belongs to you; the metropolitan region I shall take upon myself.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Ning, Zhu Chenhao, rebelled, Chongsi said to the Minister Qiao Yu, "Defense of the capital is your charge; the metropolitan region I shall take upon myself.

sentences.zh: 乃自將精兵萬人，西屯采石。

translations.literal: He then personally led ten thousand picked troops and encamped west at Caishi.
translations.idiomatic: He then personally led ten thousand picked troops and encamped to the west at Caishi.

sentences.zh: 遣使入安慶城中，令指揮楊銳等堅守。

translations.literal: He sent envoys into the city of Anqing ordering the commander Yang Rui and others to hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys into the city of Anqing ordering the commander Yang Rui and others to hold firm.

sentences.zh: 傳檄部內，聲言京邊兵十萬旦夕至，趣供餉，以紿賊。

translations.literal: He issued proclamations throughout his jurisdiction, declaring that a hundred thousand capital and frontier troops would arrive within days and urging the supply of provisions, to deceive the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: He issued proclamations throughout his jurisdiction, declaring that a hundred thousand capital and frontier troops would arrive within days and urging the supply of provisions, so as to deceive the rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊果疑懼。

translations.literal: The rebels indeed grew suspicious and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels indeed grew suspicious and fearful.

sentences.zh: 事定，兵部及巡按御史胡潔言其功。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, the ministry of war and the touring censor Hu Jie reported his merit.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was settled, the Ministry of War and the touring censor Hu Jie reported his achievements.

sentences.zh: 時已就進戶部右侍郎，乃賜敕嘉勞。

translations.literal: By then he had already been promoted to right vice minister of revenue, and an edict of commendation was bestowed upon him.
translations.idiomatic: By then he had already been promoted to Right Vice Minister of Revenue, and an edict of commendation was bestowed upon him.

sentences.zh: 有建議修蘇、松水利者，進充嗣工部尚書兼領水利事。

translations.literal: When someone proposed repairing the waterworks of Suzhou and Songjiang, Chongsi was advanced to minister of works with concurrent charge of water conservancy.
translations.idiomatic: When someone proposed repairing the waterworks of Suzhou and Songjiang, Chongsi was promoted to Minister of Works with concurrent charge of water conservancy.

sentences.zh: 未幾，世宗嗣位，遣工部郎林文霈、顏如翙佐之。

translations.literal: Before long, when the Shizong Emperor succeeded, he sent the bureau directors Lin Wenpei and Yan Ruhui to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, when Emperor Shizong succeeded to the throne, he sent the bureau directors Lin Wenpei and Yan Ruhui to assist him.

sentences.zh: 開白茅港，疏吳淞江，六閱月而訖工。

translations.literal: They opened the Baimao harbor and dredged the Wusong River; the work was completed in six months.
translations.idiomatic: They opened the Baimao harbor and dredged the Wusong River; the work was completed in six months.

sentences.zh: 語詳《河渠志》。

translations.literal: The details are given in the Treatise on Rivers and Canals.
translations.idiomatic: The details are given in the Treatise on Rivers and Canals.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖元年論平宸濠功，加太子少保。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiajing, when the merit of pacifying Chen Hao was discussed, he was given the additional title of junior mentor to the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 1, when the merit of pacifying Chenhao was discussed, he was given the additional title of Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 蘇、松白糧輸內府。

translations.literal: White grain from Suzhou and Songjiang was delivered to the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: White grain from Suzhou and Songjiang was delivered to the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 正德時驟增內使五千人，糧亦加十三萬石。

translations.literal: In the Zhengde reign the inner eunuchs were suddenly increased by five thousand men, and the grain quota was also raised by a hundred and thirty thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengde reign the inner eunuchs were suddenly increased by five thousand men, and the grain quota was also raised by a hundred and thirty thousand piculs.

sentences.zh: 帝用充嗣言，減從故額。

translations.literal: The emperor followed Chongsi's advice and reduced the quota to the former amount.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor followed Chongsi's advice and reduced the quota to the former amount.

sentences.zh: 又請常賦外盡蠲歲辦之浮額者，內府征收，監以科道官，毋縱內臣苛索。

translations.literal: He also asked that beyond the regular tax all excess amounts in annual procurement be wholly remitted, that collection for the inner palace be supervised by censorial officials, and that inner eunuchs not be allowed to exact harshly.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that beyond the regular tax all excess amounts in annual procurement be wholly remitted, that collection for the inner palace be supervised by censorial officials, and that inner eunuchs not be allowed to exact harshly.

sentences.zh: 帝俱從之。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted all of this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted all of these proposals.

sentences.zh: 尋改南京兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Shortly he was transferred to minister of war at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly he was transferred to Minister of War at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 七年致仕，卒。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he retired and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he retired from office and died.

sentences.zh: 久之，詔贈太子太保，謚康和。

translations.literal: Long afterward an edict posthumously enfeoffed him as grand mentor to the heir apparent and gave him the posthumous name Kanghe.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward an edict posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Mentor to the Heir Apparent and gave him the posthumous name Kanghe (Peaceful and Harmonious).

sentences.zh: 吳廷舉，字獻臣，其先嘉魚人，祖戍梧州，遂家焉。

translations.literal: Wu Tingju, styled Xianchen, was originally of Jiayu; his grandfather was garrisoned at Wuzhou and the family settled there.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Tingju, styled Xianchen, was originally of Jiayu; his grandfather was posted to a garrison at Wuzhou, and the family settled there.

sentences.zh: 成化二十三年登進士，除順德知縣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Chenghua he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed magistrate of Shunde.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua 23 he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed magistrate of Shunde.

sentences.zh: 上官屬修中貴人先祠，廷舉不可。

translations.literal: His superior ordered him to repair first the shrine of a favored eunuch; Tingju refused.
translations.idiomatic: His superior ordered him to repair first the shrine of a favored eunuch; Tingju refused.

sentences.zh: 市舶中官市葛，以二葛與之，曰：「非產也。」

translations.literal: The maritime-trade eunuch sought to buy ramie cloth; Tingju gave him two lengths and said, "This is not a local product.
translations.idiomatic: The maritime-trade eunuch sought to buy ramie cloth; Tingju gave him two lengths and said, "This is not a local product.

sentences.zh: 中官大怒。

translations.literal: The eunuch was greatly enraged.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch was furious.

sentences.zh: 御史汪宗器亦惡廷舉，曰：「彼專抗上官，市名耳。」

translations.literal: The censor Wang Zongqi also disliked Tingju and said, "He specializes in defying superiors merely to buy a reputation.
translations.idiomatic: The censor Wang Zongqi also disliked Tingju and said, "He specializes in defying his superiors merely to buy a reputation.

sentences.zh: 會廷舉毀淫祠二百五十所，撤其材作堤，葺學宮、書院。

translations.literal: Just then Tingju destroyed two hundred and fifty illicit shrines, used their timber to build dikes, and repaired the Confucian school and academies.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Tingju destroyed two hundred and fifty illicit shrines, used their timber to build dikes, and repaired the Confucian school and academies.

sentences.zh: 宗器謂有所侵盜，執下獄。

translations.literal: Zongqi claimed there had been embezzlement and had him thrown into prison.
translations.idiomatic: Zongqi claimed there had been embezzlement and had him thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 按之不得間，慚而止。

translations.literal: Investigation found no opening; ashamed, Zongqi stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The investigation found no opening; ashamed, Zongqi dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 為縣十年，稍遷成都同知。

translations.literal: After ten years as magistrate he was gradually transferred to be assistant prefect of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: After ten years as magistrate he was gradually transferred to assistant prefect of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 憂歸，補松江。

translations.literal: He returned home in mourning, then was reassigned to Songjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home to observe mourning, then was reassigned to Songjiang.

sentences.zh: 用尚書馬文升、劉大夏薦，擢廣東僉事。

translations.literal: On the recommendation of the ministers Ma Wensheng and Liu Daxia he was promoted to assistant surveillance commissioner of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: On the recommendation of the ministers Ma Wensheng and Liu Daxia he was promoted to assistant surveillance commissioner of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 從總督潘蕃討平南海、清遠諸盜。

translations.literal: Following the supreme commander Pan Fan he campaigned to pacify the bandits of Nanhai, Qingyuan, and other districts.
translations.idiomatic: Following the supreme commander Pan Fan he campaigned to pacify the bandits of Nanhai, Qingyuan, and other districts.

sentences.zh: 正德初，歷副使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengde he served as vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhengde reign he served as vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 發總鎮中官潘忠二十罪。

translations.literal: He exposed twenty crimes of the eunuch defender Pan Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: He exposed twenty crimes of the eunuch defender Pan Zhong.

sentences.zh: 忠亦訐廷舉他事，逮系詔獄。

translations.literal: Zhong in turn accused Tingju of other matters, and he was seized and thrown into the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong in turn accused Tingju of other matters, and he was seized and thrown into the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾矯詔，枷之十余日，幾死。

translations.literal: Liu Jin forged an edict and had him cangued for more than ten days, nearly to death.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin forged an edict and had him cangued for more than ten days, nearly to the point of death.

sentences.zh: 戍雁門，旋赦免。

translations.literal: He was exiled to Yanmen, then soon pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: He was exiled to Yanmen, then soon pardoned.

sentences.zh: 楊一清薦其才，擢江西右參政。

translations.literal: Yang Yiqing recommended his talent, and he was promoted to right assistant administration commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yiqing recommended his talent, and he was promoted to Right Assistant Administration Commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 敗華林賊於連河。

translations.literal: He defeated the Hualin bandits at Lianhe.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated the Hualin bandits at Lianhe.

sentences.zh: 從陳金大破姚源賊。

translations.literal: Following Chen Jin he inflicted a great defeat on the bandits of Yaoyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Following Chen Jin he inflicted a great defeat on the bandits of Yaoyuan.

sentences.zh: 其黨走裴源，復從俞諫破之。

translations.literal: Their partisans fled to Peiyuan; he again followed Yu Jian and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Their partisans fled to Peiyuan; he again followed Yu Jian and defeated them there.

sentences.zh: 賊首胡浩三既撫復叛，廷舉往諭，為所執。

translations.literal: The bandit leader Hu Haosan, having submitted to pacification, rebelled again; Tingju went to admonish him and was seized.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit leader Hu Haosan, having submitted to pacification, rebelled again; Tingju went to admonish him and was taken captive.

sentences.zh: 居三月，盡得其要領，誘使攜。

translations.literal: After three months he had learned all their secrets and induced defections among them.
translations.idiomatic: After three months he had learned all their secrets and induced defections among them.

sentences.zh: 及得還，浩三果殺其兄浩二，內亂。

translations.literal: When he was able to return, Haosan indeed killed his elder brother Haoer, and internal strife broke out.
translations.idiomatic: When he was able to return, Haosan indeed killed his elder brother Haoer, and internal strife broke out.

sentences.zh: 官兵乘之，遂擒浩三。

translations.literal: Government troops seized the opportunity and captured Haosan.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops seized the opportunity and captured Haosan.

sentences.zh: 與副使李夢陽不協，奏夢陽侵官，因乞休。

translations.literal: He was at odds with the vice commissioner Li Mengyang, memorialized that Mengyang had overstepped his authority, and asked to retire.
translations.idiomatic: He was at odds with the vice commissioner Li Mengyang, memorialized that Mengyang had overstepped his authority, and asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 不俟命竟去，坐停一歲俸。

translations.literal: Without awaiting permission he left his post and was penalized by suspension of one year's salary.
translations.idiomatic: Without awaiting permission he left his post and was penalized by suspension of one year's salary.

sentences.zh: 起廣東右布政使，復佐陳金平府江賊。

translations.literal: He was recalled as right administration commissioner of Guangdong and again assisted Chen Jin in pacifying the bandits of Fujiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Right Administration Commissioner of Guangdong and again assisted Chen Jin in pacifying the bandits of Fujiang.

sentences.zh: 擢右副都御史，振湖廣饑。

translations.literal: He was promoted to right censor-in-chief and provided relief for the famine in Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief and provided relief for the famine in Huguang.

sentences.zh: 已，復出湖南定諸夷疆地。

translations.literal: Later he went out again to Hunan to fix the borderlands of various tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Later he went out again to Hunan to fix the borderlands of the various tribes.

sentences.zh: 寧王宸濠有逆謀，疏陳江西軍政六事，為豫防計。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Ning, Chen Hao, harbored treasonous designs, he memorialized six matters of Jiangxi military administration as measures of precaution.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Ning, Zhu Chenhao, harbored treasonous designs, he memorialized six matters of Jiangxi military administration as precautionary measures.

sentences.zh: 世宗立，召為工部右侍郎，旋改兵部。

translations.literal: When the Shizong Emperor ascended the throne, Tingju was summoned as right vice minister of works, then soon transferred to the ministry of war.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong ascended the throne, Tingju was summoned as Right Vice Minister of Works, then soon transferred to the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 上疏詆陸完、王瓊、梁儲及少傅蔣冕，而自以為己昔居憲職無一言，乞罷黜以儆幸位。

translations.literal: He memorialized denouncing Lu Wan, Wang Qiong, Liang Chu, and the junior mentor Jiang Mian, while declaring that he himself, though once in a censorial post, had not spoken a word and begged dismissal to warn those who held office by luck.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized denouncing Lu Wan, Wang Qiong, Liang Chu, and the Junior Mentor Jiang Mian, while declaring that he himself, though once in a censorial post, had not spoken a word and begged dismissal to warn those who held office by luck.

sentences.zh: 時完早得罪，瓊及儲已罷去，廷舉借以傾冕。

translations.literal: By then Wan had long since been punished, and Qiong and Chu had already been dismissed; Tingju used this to bring down Mian.
translations.idiomatic: By then Wan had long since been punished, and Qiong and Chu had already been dismissed; Tingju used the occasion to bring down Mian.

sentences.zh: 冕遂求罷。

translations.literal: Mian thereupon asked to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Mian thereupon asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 帝頗不直廷舉，調南京工部，而慰諭冕。

translations.literal: The emperor was rather displeased with Tingju, transferred him to the ministry of works at Nanjing, and comforted Mian.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was rather displeased with Tingju, transferred him to the Ministry of Works at Nanjing, and comforted Mian.

sentences.zh: 冕固請留之，不聽。

translations.literal: Mian firmly asked that Tingju be kept, but the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Mian firmly asked that Tingju be kept, but the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖元年，廷舉乞休。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiajing Tingju asked to retire.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 1 Tingju asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 尋以災異復自劾求罷，勸帝修德應天，因奏行其部興革十二事。

translations.literal: Soon, citing omens and disasters, he again impeached himself and asked to resign, urging the emperor to cultivate virtue in response to Heaven and memorializing twelve reforms for his ministry to carry out.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, citing omens and disasters, he again impeached himself and asked to resign, urging the emperor to cultivate virtue in response to Heaven and memorializing twelve reforms for his ministry to carry out.

sentences.zh: 尋就改戶部，遷右都御史，巡撫應天諸府。

translations.literal: Shortly he was transferred to the ministry of revenue, then promoted to right censor-in-chief and made grand coordinator of Yingtian and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly he was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue, then promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief and made Grand Coordinator of Yingtian and the other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 長洲知縣郭波以事挫織造中官張誌聰。

translations.literal: Guo Bo, magistrate of Changzhou, on some matter thwarted the weaving-office eunuch Zhang Zhicong.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Bo, magistrate of Changzhou, on some matter thwarted the weaving-office eunuch Zhang Zhicong.

sentences.zh: 誌聰伺波出，倒曳之車後。

translations.literal: Zhicong waited until Bo came out and dragged him head-down behind a cart.
translations.idiomatic: Zhicong waited until Bo came out and dragged him head-down behind a cart.

sentences.zh: 典史蕭景腆操兵教場，急率兵救。

translations.literal: The clerical assistant Xiao Jingtian was drilling troops on the parade ground and hurriedly led soldiers to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: The clerical assistant Xiao Jingtian was drilling troops on the parade ground and hurriedly led soldiers to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 百姓登屋，飛瓦擊誌聰。

translations.literal: The common people climbed onto roofs and hurled tiles at Zhicong.
translations.idiomatic: The common people climbed onto roofs and hurled tiles at Zhicong.

sentences.zh: 誌聰奏逮波、景腆，廷舉具白誌聰貪黷狀。

translations.literal: Zhicong memorialized to have Bo and Jingtian arrested; Tingju fully reported Zhicong's corrupt conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Zhicong memorialized to have Bo and Jingtian arrested; Tingju fully reported Zhicong's corrupt conduct.

sentences.zh: 帝乃降波五級，調景腆遠方，誌聰亦召還。

translations.literal: The emperor then demoted Bo five ranks, transferred Jingtian to a distant post, and recalled Zhicong as well.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then demoted Bo five ranks, transferred Jingtian to a distant post, and recalled Zhicong as well.

sentences.zh: 三年，以「大禮」議未定，請如洪武中修《孝慈錄》故事，令兩京部、寺、臺、省及天下督、撫各條所見，並詢家居老臣，采而行之，匯為一書，以詔後世。

translations.literal: In the third year, because the Grand Rites debate was unsettled, he asked that, following the Hongwu precedent of compiling the Record of Filial Piety and Kindness, the ministries, directorates, censorates, and provincial offices of both capitals and all grand coordinators throughout the empire each set forth their views, and that retired elder statesmen also be consulted; the results were to be gathered into one book to instruct posterity.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, because the Grand Rites debate was still unsettled, he asked that, following the Hongwu precedent of compiling the Record of Filial Piety and Kindness, the ministries, directorates, censorates, and provincial offices of both capitals and all grand coordinators throughout the empire each set forth their views, and that retired elder statesmen also be consulted; the results were to be gathered into one book to instruct posterity.

sentences.zh: 時已定稱本生考，廷舉窺帝意不慊，故為此奏。

translations.literal: By then the title for the emperor's biological father had already been fixed; Tingju perceived that the emperor was not satisfied and therefore made this memorial.
translations.idiomatic: By then the title for the emperor's biological father had already been fixed; Tingju perceived that the emperor was not satisfied and therefore made this memorial.

sentences.zh: 給事中張原、劉祺交劾之，不報。

translations.literal: The supervising secretaries Zhang Yuan and Liu Qi jointly impeached him, but no reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising secretaries Zhang Yuan and Liu Qi jointly impeached him, but no reply was given.

sentences.zh: 尋改南京工部尚書，辭不拜，稱疾乞休。

translations.literal: Shortly he was transferred to minister of works at Nanjing, declined to accept the appointment, and pleaded illness to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly he was transferred to Minister of Works at Nanjing, declined to accept the appointment, and pleaded illness to retire.

sentences.zh: 帝慰留。

translations.literal: The emperor comforted him and kept him in office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor comforted him and kept him in office.

sentences.zh: 已，復辭，且引白居易、張詠詩，語多詼諧，中復用嗚呼字。

translations.literal: Later he resigned again, citing poems by Bai Juyi and Zhang Yong; his language was largely jocular, and he again used the word "Alas."
translations.idiomatic: Later he resigned again, citing poems by Bai Juyi and Zhang Yong; his language was largely jocular, and he again used the word "Alas."

sentences.zh: 帝怒，以廷舉怨望無人臣禮，勒致仕。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, deeming that Tingju harbored resentment and lacked the deportment of a subject, and compelled him to retire.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry, deeming that Tingju harbored resentment and lacked the deportment of a subject, and compelled him to retire.

sentences.zh: 廷舉面如削瓜。

translations.literal: Tingju's face was like a peeled melon.
translations.idiomatic: Tingju's face was lean as a peeled melon.

sentences.zh: 衣敝帶穿，不事藻飾。

translations.literal: His clothes were worn and his belt frayed; he did not attend to ornament.
translations.idiomatic: His clothes were worn and his belt frayed; he did not attend to ornament.

sentences.zh: 言行必自信，人莫能奪。

translations.literal: In word and deed he always trusted himself, and no one could sway him.
translations.idiomatic: In word and deed he always trusted himself, and no one could sway him.

sentences.zh: 其在太學時，兄事羅玘。

translations.literal: When he was at the National University he treated Luo Qin as an elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: When he was at the National University he treated Luo Qin as an elder brother.

sentences.zh: 玘病痢，仆死，自煮藥飲之。

translations.literal: When Qin fell ill with dysentery and his servant died, Tingju himself brewed medicine and gave it to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin fell ill with dysentery and his servant died, Tingju himself brewed medicine and gave it to him.

sentences.zh: 負以如廁，一晝夜數十反。

translations.literal: He carried him to the privy dozens of times in a day and night.
translations.idiomatic: He carried him to the privy dozens of times in a day and night.

sentences.zh: 玘嘗語人曰：「獻臣生我。」

translations.literal: Qin once said to others, "Xianchen gave me life.
translations.idiomatic: Qin once said to others, "Xianchen gave me life.

sentences.zh: 廷舉好薛瑄、胡居仁學，尊事陳獻章。

translations.literal: Tingju admired the learning of Xue Xuan and Hu Juren and honored Chen Xianzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Tingju admired the learning of Xue Xuan and Hu Juren and honored Chen Xianzhang.

sentences.zh: 居湫隘，亡郭外田，有書萬卷。

translations.literal: He lived in cramped quarters, owned no fields outside the city wall, and had ten thousand volumes of books.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in cramped quarters, owned no fields outside the city wall, and had ten thousand volumes of books.

sentences.zh: 及卒，總督姚鏌庀其喪。

translations.literal: When he died, the supreme commander Yao Mo arranged his funeral.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, the supreme commander Yao Mo arranged his funeral.

sentences.zh: 隆慶中，追謚清惠。

translations.literal: In the Longqing reign he was posthumously given the name Qinghui.
translations.idiomatic: In the Longqing reign he was posthumously given the name Qinghui (Pure and Kind).

sentences.zh: 弟廷弼，舉於鄉。

translations.literal: His younger brother Tingbi passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Tingbi passed the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 廷舉枷吏部前，廷弼臥其械下。

translations.literal: When Tingju was cangued before the ministry of personnel, Tingbi lay beneath the cangue.
translations.idiomatic: When Tingju was cangued before the Ministry of Personnel, Tingbi lay beneath the cangue.

sentences.zh: 刑部主事宿進為奏記張糸采，乃得釋。

translations.literal: The principal secretary Su Jin of the ministry of punishments submitted a letter to Zhang Cai on his behalf, and he was released.
translations.idiomatic: The principal secretary Su Jin of the Ministry of Punishments submitted a letter to Zhang Cai on his behalf, and he was released.

sentences.zh: 方良永，字壽卿，莆田人。

translations.literal: Fang Liangyong, styled Shouqing, was a man of Putian.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Liangyong, styled Shouqing, was a native of Putian.

sentences.zh: 弘治三年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the third year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Hongzhi 3.

sentences.zh: 督逋兩廣，峻卻饋遺，為布政使劉大夏所器。

translations.literal: While supervising arrears in the two Guang provinces he sternly refused gifts and was valued by the administration commissioner Liu Daxia.
translations.idiomatic: While supervising arrears in the two Guang provinces he sternly refused gifts and was valued by the administration commissioner Liu Daxia.

sentences.zh: 還授刑部主事。

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed a principal secretary in the ministry of punishments.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed a principal secretary in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 進員外郎，擢廣東僉事。

translations.literal: He was advanced to vice director and promoted to assistant surveillance commissioner of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to vice director and promoted to assistant surveillance commissioner of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 瓊州賊符南蛇為亂，大夏時為總督，檄攝海南兵備，會師討平之。

translations.literal: The bandit Fu Nanshe of Qiongzhou rose in rebellion; Daxia was then supreme commander and ordered Liangyong to take charge of Hainan military defense; their forces joined and the rebels were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit Fu Nanshe of Qiongzhou rose in rebellion; Daxia was then supreme commander and ordered Liangyong to take charge of Hainan military defense; their forces joined and the rebels were pacified.

sentences.zh: 御史坐良永失利。

translations.literal: A censor held Liangyong responsible for a defeat.
translations.idiomatic: A censor held Liangyong responsible for a defeat.

sentences.zh: 大夏已入為本兵，為白於朝，賚銀幣。

translations.literal: Daxia had already entered the capital as minister of war and cleared the matter at court; Liangyong was rewarded with silver and silks.
translations.idiomatic: Daxia had already entered the capital as Minister of War and cleared the matter at court; Liangyong was rewarded with silver and silks.

sentences.zh: 正德初，父喪除，待銓闕下。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengde, after the mourning for his father was completed, he waited at the ministry gate for appointment.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhengde reign, after the mourning for his father was completed, he waited at the ministry gate for appointment.

sentences.zh: 外官朝見畢，必謁劉瑾。

translations.literal: When officials from outside the capital had finished their audience, they invariably called on Liu Jin.
translations.idiomatic: After provincial officials had finished their audience at court, they invariably paid a call on Liu Jin.

sentences.zh: 鴻臚導良永詣左順門叩頭畢，令東向揖瑾，良永竟出。

translations.literal: The director of ceremonial guided Liangyong to the Left Gate of Correct Deportment; when the kowtow was finished, he was told to bow toward the east to Jin, but Liangyong went straight out.
translations.idiomatic: The director of ceremonial led Liangyong to the Left Gate of Correct Deportment; after he had kowtowed, they told him to bow east toward Jin, but Liangyong walked straight out.

sentences.zh: 或勸詣瑾家，良永不可。

translations.literal: Some urged him to call at Jin's house; Liangyong would not.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged him to call at Jin's residence, but Liangyong refused.

sentences.zh: 及吏部除良永河南撫民僉事，中旨勒致仕。

translations.literal: When the ministry of personnel appointed Liangyong assistant administration commissioner for pacifying the people in Henan, an imperial rescript ordered him to retire.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ministry of Personnel appointed Liangyong assistant administration commissioner for pacifying the people in Henan, an imperial rescript compelled him to retire.

sentences.zh: 既去，瑾怒未已，欲假海南殺人事中之。

translations.literal: After he had left, Jin's anger had not ceased; he wished to use a homicide case in Hainan to trap him in it.
translations.idiomatic: After Liangyong had left office, Jin's anger had not abated; he wished to use a homicide case in Hainan to entangle him in it.

sentences.zh: 刑部郎中周敏力持，乃不坐。

translations.literal: Zhou Min, a bureau director in the ministry of punishments, firmly held out, and Liangyong was not convicted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Min, a bureau director in the Ministry of Punishments, firmly resisted, and Liangyong was not convicted.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，起湖廣副使。

translations.literal: When Jin was executed, Liangyong was reinstated as vice commissioner of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin was executed, Liangyong was reinstated as vice commissioner of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 尋擢廣西按察使。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted surveillance commissioner of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to surveillance commissioner of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 發巡按御史朱誌榮罪至謫戍。

translations.literal: He exposed the crimes of touring censor Zhu Zhirong to the point of banishment to military service.
translations.idiomatic: He exposed touring censor Zhu Zhirong's crimes to the point that Zhu was banished to frontier garrison duty.

sentences.zh: 遷山東右布政使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be right administration commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as right administration commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 旋調浙江，改左。

translations.literal: He was soon transferred to Zhejiang and changed to the left post.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Zhejiang and appointed left administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 錢寧以鈔二萬鬻於浙，良永上疏曰：「四方盜甫息，瘡痍未瘳，浙東西雨雹。

translations.literal: Qian Ning sold twenty thousand notes in Zhejiang; Liangyong memorialized, saying: "Bandits in the four quarters have only just been stilled, the wounds are not yet healed, and east and west Zhejiang have been struck by hail.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Ning sold twenty thousand paper notes in Zhejiang; Liangyong memorialized, saying: "Banditry in the realm has only just subsided, the land is still scarred by war, and hail has struck both eastern and western Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 寧廝養賤流，假義子名，躋公侯之列。

translations.literal: Ning is a menial groom of base origin who, under the name of adopted son, has ascended to the ranks of dukes and marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Ning is a menial groom of base birth who, under the title of adopted son, has risen to the ranks of dukes and marquises.

sentences.zh: 賜予無算，納賄不貲，乃敢攫民財，戕邦本。

translations.literal: His gifts are beyond counting, his bribes beyond measure, yet he dares seize the people's wealth and harm the foundation of the state.
translations.idiomatic: He has received gifts beyond reckoning and bribes beyond measure, yet he dares seize the people's wealth and wound the foundations of the state.

sentences.zh: 有司奉行急於詔旨，胥吏緣為奸，椎膚剝髓，民不堪命。

translations.literal: The responsible offices carry out orders more urgently than the edict itself; clerks use this as a pretext for villainy, flaying skin and stripping marrow, and the people cannot bear the burden.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials enforce the order even more harshly than the edict requires; clerks seize the chance for corruption, squeezing the people dry, until the common folk can no longer endure it.

sentences.zh: 鎮守太監王堂、劉璟畏寧威，受役使。

translations.literal: The garrison eunuchs Wang Tang and Liu Jing fear Ning's power and submit to his orders.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison eunuchs Wang Tang and Liu Jing fear Ning's power and do his bidding.

sentences.zh: 臣何敢愛一死，不以聞。

translations.literal: How dare your servant cherish his life and not report this?
translations.idiomatic: How could I value my own life and fail to report this to Your Majesty?

sentences.zh: 乞陛下下寧詔獄，明正典刑，並治其黨，以謝百姓。」

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty to send Ning to prison by edict, apply the statutes openly, and punish his faction as well, to answer to the people."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to send Ning to prison by edict, punish him according to law, and deal with his followers as well, so as to give satisfaction to the people."

sentences.zh: 寧懼，留疏不下。

translations.literal: Ning was afraid and kept the memorial from being transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: Ning was afraid and kept the memorial from being forwarded.

sentences.zh: 謀遣校尉捕假勢鬻鈔者，以自飾於帝，而請以鈔直還之民，陰召還前所遣使。

translations.literal: He plotted to send guards to arrest those who sold notes by borrowing his power, to adorn himself before the emperor, and to request that the value of the notes be returned to the people, while secretly recalling the agents he had earlier sent out.
translations.idiomatic: He plotted to send guards to arrest those who had sold notes under borrowed authority from him, so as to make himself look good before the emperor, to ask that the notes' value be returned to the people, and secretly to recall the agents he had earlier dispatched.

sentences.zh: 寧初欲散鈔遍天下，先行之浙江、山東，山東為巡撫趙璜所格，而良永白髮其奸，寧自是不敢鬻鈔矣。

translations.literal: Ning had at first wished to spread the notes throughout the realm; he first tried it in Zhejiang and Shandong. Shandong was blocked by grand coordinator Zhao Huang, while Liangyong openly exposed his treachery, and from then on Ning did not dare sell notes.
translations.idiomatic: Ning had at first intended to circulate the notes throughout the empire, beginning in Zhejiang and Shandong. In Shandong, grand coordinator Zhao Huang blocked him, while Liangyong openly exposed his scheme; from then on Ning no longer dared sell the notes.

sentences.zh: 寧方得誌，公卿、臺諫無敢出一語。

translations.literal: Ning had just had his way; among grand secretaries, ministers, and censorial officials none dared utter a word.
translations.idiomatic: Ning was then at the height of his power, and among grand secretaries, ministers, and censorial officials none dared speak out.

sentences.zh: 良永以外僚訟言誅之，聞者震悚。

translations.literal: Liangyong, as an outside official, accused him in a memorial calling for his execution; those who heard it were shaken with fear.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyong, an outside official, memorialized calling for his execution; all who heard of it were shaken with fear.

sentences.zh: 良永念母老，恐中禍，三疏乞休去。

translations.literal: Liangyong thought of his aged mother, feared falling into disaster, and thrice memorialized requesting retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyong, mindful that his mother was old and fearing he might come to harm, submitted three memorials requesting retirement.

sentences.zh: 良永侍父疾，衣不解帶者三月。

translations.literal: When Liangyong attended his father's illness, for three months he did not undo his belt.
translations.idiomatic: While nursing his father's illness, Liangyong did not remove his belt for three months.

sentences.zh: 母病，良永年六十余矣，手進湯藥無少怠。

translations.literal: When his mother fell ill, though Liangyong was already more than sixty, he personally presented broth and medicine without the least slackening.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother fell ill, though Liangyong was already over sixty, he personally brought her medicine and broth without the slightest neglect.

sentences.zh: 居倚廬哀毀，稱純孝焉。

translations.literal: He dwelt in the mourning hut with grief that wasted the body, and was called a model of pure filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He mourned in the mourning hut with such grief that it wasted his body, and he was acclaimed as a model of pure filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 素善王守仁，而論學與之異。

translations.literal: He had long been on good terms with Wang Shouren, but his views on learning differed from his.
translations.idiomatic: He had long been friendly with Wang Yangming, but his views on learning differed from Wang's.

sentences.zh: 嘗語人曰：「近世專言心學，自謂超悟獨到，推其說以自附於象山，而上達於孔子。

translations.literal: He once said to others: "In recent times men speak only of the learning of the mind, claiming transcendent enlightenment and originality of their own, and extend their doctrine to attach themselves to Xiangshan and reach up to Confucius.
translations.idiomatic: He once said to others: "In recent times men speak only of the learning of the mind, claiming a unique enlightenment of their own, and extend their doctrine to align themselves with Lu Jiuyuan and even with Confucius.

sentences.zh: 目賢聖教人次第為小子無用之學，程、朱而下無不受擯，而不知其入於妄。」

translations.literal: They regard the successive teachings of sages and worthies as the useless learning of petty youths; from Cheng and Zhu downward none escape rejection, yet they do not know that they have entered delusion."
translations.idiomatic: They treat the successive teachings of the sages as childish and useless learning; from the Cheng brothers and Zhu Xi downward none escape their rejection, yet they do not realize that they have fallen into delusion."

sentences.zh: 弟良節，官廣東左布政使，亦有治行。

translations.literal: His younger brother Liangjie served as left administration commissioner of Guangdong and likewise had a record of good governance.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Liangjie served as left administration commissioner of Guangdong and likewise had a reputation for effective administration.

sentences.zh: 子重傑，舉於鄉，以孝聞。

translations.literal: His son Chongjie passed the provincial examination and was known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chongjie passed the provincial examination and was known for his filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 王爌，字存納，黃巖人。

translations.literal: Wang Kuang, styled Cunna, was a man of Huangyan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kuang, styled Cunna, was a native of Huangyan.

sentences.zh: 弘治十五年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifteenth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Hongzhi 15.

sentences.zh: 除太常博士。

translations.literal: He was appointed erudite of the court of imperial sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed an erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 正德時，屢遷刑科都給事中。

translations.literal: In the Zhengde reign he was repeatedly promoted to supervising secretary of the punishments section.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengde reign he was repeatedly promoted until he became supervising secretary of the punishments section.

sentences.zh: 武定侯郭勛鎮兩廣，行事乖謬。

translations.literal: The Marquis of Wuding, Guo Xun, garrisoned the two Guang provinces and conducted affairs perversely.
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Wuding, Guo Xun, commanded the two Guang provinces and conducted affairs in an arbitrary and improper manner.

sentences.zh: 詔自陳，勛強辨，爌等駁之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to state his own case; Xun argued forcefully, and Kuang and others rebutted him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered him to submit a personal account; Xun argued forcefully, and Kuang and others rebutted him.

sentences.zh: 都察院覆奏，不錄爌言，爌並劾都御史彭澤。

translations.literal: The censorate memorialized in reply but did not record Kuang's words; Kuang also impeached the censor-in-chief Peng Ze.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate memorialized in reply but did not include Kuang's statements; Kuang also impeached the censor-in-chief Peng Ze.

sentences.zh: 帝責澤，置勛不問。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked Ze and left Xun unpunished.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked Peng Ze and took no action against Xun.

sentences.zh: 御史林有年直言下獄，浙江僉事韓邦奇忤中官被逮，爌皆救之。

translations.literal: The censor Lin Younian was imprisoned for blunt speech; Han Bangqi, assistant surveillance commissioner of Zhejiang, offended a eunuch and was arrested; Kuang rescued them both.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Lin Younian was imprisoned for speaking bluntly; Han Bangqi, assistant surveillance commissioner of Zhejiang, offended a eunuch and was arrested; Kuang intervened to save them both.

sentences.zh: 帝幸大同久不反，爌力請回鸞。

translations.literal: The emperor sojourned at Datong for a long time without returning; Kuang urgently requested that the imperial carriage return.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor stayed at Datong for a long time without returning; Kuang urgently petitioned for the imperial tour to end and the court to return.

sentences.zh: 又與工科石天柱救彭澤，忤王瓊。

translations.literal: He also joined Shi Tianzhu of the works section in rescuing Peng Ze, offending Wang Qiong.
translations.idiomatic: He also joined Shi Tianzhu of the works section in defending Peng Ze, thereby offending Wang Qiong.

sentences.zh: 中旨調兩人於外，爌得惠州推官。

translations.literal: An imperial rescript transferred the two men to posts outside the capital; Kuang received the post of magistrate of Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial rescript transferred the two men to posts outside the capital; Kuang was assigned as magistrate of Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 世宗立，召復都給事中。

translations.literal: When Shizong ascended the throne, Kuang was recalled to his former post as supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiajing emperor ascended the throne, Kuang was recalled as supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 旋擢太仆少卿，改太常。

translations.literal: He was soon promoted vice minister of the court of the imperial stud and then transferred to the court of imperial sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and then transferred to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三年遷應天府尹。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiajing he was transferred to be prefect of Yingtian.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 3 he was transferred to serve as prefect of Yingtian.

sentences.zh: 歲大祲，奏免其賦。

translations.literal: That year there was a great famine; he memorialized to remit the taxes.
translations.idiomatic: That year there was a severe famine; he memorialized for tax relief.

sentences.zh: 居四年，遷南京刑部右侍郎，以母老歸養。

translations.literal: After four years he was transferred to be right vice minister of punishments at Nanjing and returned home to support his aged mother.
translations.idiomatic: After four years he was transferred to right vice minister of punishments at Nanjing and returned home to care for his aged mother.

sentences.zh: 家居十年，起故官。

translations.literal: He lived at home for ten years, then was reinstated in his former office.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in retirement for ten years, then was reinstated in his former post.

sentences.zh: 尋擢南京右都御史。

translations.literal: He was soon promoted right censor-in-chief at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to right censor-in-chief at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 守備中官進表，率以兩御史監禮。

translations.literal: When the garrison eunuch presented a memorial, he routinely had two censors oversee the ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: When the garrison eunuch presented a memorial, he routinely had two censors supervise the ceremony.

sentences.zh: 爌曰：「中官安得役御史？」

translations.literal: Kuang said: "How may a eunuch command censors?"
translations.idiomatic: Kuang said: "How can a eunuch order censors about?"

sentences.zh: 止之。

translations.literal: He stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: He put a stop to the practice.

sentences.zh: 舉賀入朝，謁內閣夏言。

translations.literal: On being recommended for congratulations at court, he called on Grand Secretary Xia Yan in the inner cabinet.
translations.idiomatic: On entering court he called on Grand Secretary Xia Yan.

sentences.zh: 言倨甚，大臣多隅坐，爌獨引坐正之。

translations.literal: Yan was very haughty; most grand ministers sat in a corner, but Kuang alone drew him to sit in the place of honor.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was extremely arrogant; most senior ministers sat off to the side, but Kuang alone drew him to the seat of honor.

sentences.zh: 言不悅，爌遂謝病歸。

translations.literal: Yan was displeased, and Kuang thereupon resigned on grounds of illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Yan took offense, and Kuang thereupon resigned on grounds of illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 爌與御史潘壯不相能。

translations.literal: Kuang and the censor Pan Zhuang were not on good terms.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang and censor Pan Zhuang were on bad terms.

sentences.zh: 壯坐大獄，詔爌提問。

translations.literal: Zhuang was implicated in a major case, and an edict ordered Kuang to conduct the interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuang was implicated in a major case, an edict ordered Kuang to conduct the interrogation.

sentences.zh: 爌力白壯罪，至忤旨。

translations.literal: Kuang vigorously declared Zhuang innocent, even to the point of defying the imperial will.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang vigorously declared Zhuang innocent, even to the point of defying the emperor's intent.

sentences.zh: 人以此稱爌長者。

translations.literal: People for this reason called Kuang a man of magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: People for this reason praised Kuang as a man of magnanimous character.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously enfeoffed as minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously ennobled as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 王軏，開平衛人，弘治十二年進士。

translations.literal: Wang Yue was a man of Kaiping Guard and passed the jinshi examination in the twelfth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yue was a native of Kaiping Guard and passed the jinshi examination in Hongzhi 12.

sentences.zh: 正德初，歷工部員外郎，屢遷山東左布政使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengde he served as vice director in the ministry of works and was repeatedly promoted until he became left administration commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhengde reign he served as vice director in the Ministry of Works and was repeatedly promoted until he became left administration commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，入為順天府尹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiajing he entered the capital as prefect of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jiajing reign he entered the capital as prefect of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 房山地震，軏言召災有由，語多指斥。

translations.literal: When Fangshan suffered an earthquake, Yue said the calamity had its cause and his words largely pointed blame.
translations.idiomatic: When Fangshan suffered an earthquake, Yue said the calamity had its cause and his memorial largely cast blame.

sentences.zh: 忤旨切責。

translations.literal: He offended the imperial will and was sharply rebuked.
translations.idiomatic: He offended the emperor and was sharply rebuked.

sentences.zh: 尋遷副都御史，巡撫四川。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to vice censor-in-chief and appointed grand coordinator of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 芒部土官知府隴慰死，庶子政與嫡子壽爭立，朝議立壽。

translations.literal: The native-official prefect Long Wei of the Mang tribe died; the secondary son Zheng and the legitimate son Shou contended for the succession, and court deliberation favored installing Shou.
translations.idiomatic: The Mang tribal native-official prefect Long Wei died; the secondary son Zheng and the legitimate son Shou contested the succession, and court deliberation favored installing Shou.

sentences.zh: 政倚烏撒，數構兵，使人誘殺壽，奪其印。

translations.literal: Zheng relied on Wusa, repeatedly raised troops, had men lure and kill Shou, and seized his seal.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng relied on Wusa, repeatedly raised troops, had men lure Shou to his death, and seized the official seal.

sentences.zh: 軏請討之。

translations.literal: Yue requested a punitive campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: Yue requested a punitive campaign against Zheng.

sentences.zh: 乃會貴州兵分道進，擒政於水西，招降四十九寨。

translations.literal: He then joined Guizhou troops in advancing by separate routes, captured Zheng at Shuixi, and won the surrender of forty-nine stockades.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined forces with Guizhou troops advancing by separate routes, captured Zheng at Shuixi, and won the surrender of forty-nine stockades.

sentences.zh: 璽書獎勞。

translations.literal: An imperial letter commended and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent an imperial letter commending and rewarding him.

sentences.zh: 時將營仁壽宮，就拜軏工部右侍郎，督采大木。

translations.literal: As the Renshou Palace was about to be built, Yue was appointed on the spot right vice minister of works to supervise the procurement of large timber.
translations.idiomatic: As work was about to begin on the Renshou Palace, Yue was appointed on the spot right vice minister of works to supervise the procurement of large timber.

sentences.zh: 工罷，召還，改戶部。

translations.literal: When the work was finished he was recalled and transferred to the ministry of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was finished he was recalled and transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 核九門苜蓿地，以余地歸之民。

translations.literal: He audited the alfalfa lands of the nine gates and returned the surplus land to the people.
translations.idiomatic: He audited the alfalfa lands of the nine gates and returned surplus land to the people.

sentences.zh: 勘禦馬監草場，厘地二萬余頃，募民以佃。

translations.literal: He surveyed the pasturage of the imperial stud directorate, rectified more than twenty thousand qing of land, and recruited people to farm it as tenants.
translations.idiomatic: He surveyed the Imperial Stud Directorate pasturage, rectified more than twenty thousand qing of land, and recruited tenants to farm it.

sentences.zh: 房山民以牧馬地獻中官韋恒，軏厘歸之官。

translations.literal: The people of Fangshan presented horse-pasture land to the eunuch Wei Heng; Yue rectified the matter and returned it to the state.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Fangshan presented horse-pasture land to the eunuch Wei Heng; Yue rectified the matter and returned the land to official control.

sentences.zh: 奸人馮賢等復獻中官李秀，秀為請於帝，軏抗疏劾之。

translations.literal: The scoundrels Feng Xian and others again presented land to the eunuch Li Xiu; Xiu petitioned the emperor on their behalf, and Yue submitted a defiant memorial impeaching him.
translations.idiomatic: Schemers such as Feng Xian again presented land to the eunuch Li Xiu; Xiu petitioned the emperor on their behalf, and Yue submitted a forceful memorial impeaching him.

sentences.zh: 帝雖宥秀，竟治賢等如律。

translations.literal: Although the emperor pardoned Xiu, he ultimately punished Feng Xian and the others according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Although the emperor pardoned Li Xiu, he ultimately punished Feng Xian and the others according to law.

sentences.zh: 出核勛戚莊田，請如周制，計品秩，別親疏，以定多寡，非詔賜而隱占者俱追斷。

translations.literal: He went out to audit the estate lands of meritorious nobles and imperial kin, requesting that, as in the Zhou system, rank be calculated and closeness of kinship distinguished to determine how much each might hold, and that all who had concealed occupation without edictal grant be pursued and stripped.
translations.idiomatic: He went out to audit the estate lands of meritorious nobles and imperial kin, proposing that, as under the Zhou system, rank and degree of kinship should determine how much each might hold, and that all who had seized land without an edictal grant be pursued and stripped of it.

sentences.zh: 戶部尚書梁材采其言，兼並者悉歸官。

translations.literal: Minister of Revenue Liang Cai adopted his proposal, and all who had seized land by merger had it returned to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Revenue Liang Cai adopted his proposal, and all illegally consolidated lands were returned to official control.

sentences.zh: 稍進左侍郎。

translations.literal: He was soon advanced to left vice minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to left vice minister.

sentences.zh: 初，軏之平隴政也，以隴氏無後，請改設流官，兵部尚書李鉞等然之。

translations.literal: When Yue had earlier pacified Long Zheng, because the Long house had no heir he requested that a regular official be installed instead; Minister of War Li Zhen and others agreed.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue had earlier pacified Long Zheng, because the Long house had no heir he requested that regular officials be installed instead; Minister of War Li Zhen and others agreed.

sentences.zh: 遂改芒部為鎮雄府，分置四長官司，授隴氏疏屬阿濟等為長官，而擢重慶通判程洸為試知府。

translations.literal: Mang territory was therefore changed to Zhenxiong Prefecture, four native-official districts of chiefs were established, distant kinsmen of the Long house such as Aji were appointed chiefs, and Chongqing subprefect Cheng Hao was promoted to acting prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Mang territory was therefore reorganized as Zhenxiong Prefecture, four chiefdom districts were established, distant kinsmen of the Long house such as Aji were appointed chiefs, and Chongqing subprefect Cheng Hao was promoted to acting prefect.

sentences.zh: 隴氏舊部沙保等攻執洸，奪其印，欲復立隴氏後。

translations.literal: Former followers of the Long house such as Shabao attacked, seized Cheng Hao, and took his seal, wishing to restore a descendant of the Long house.
translations.idiomatic: Former followers of the Long house such as Shabao attacked, seized Cheng Hao, and took his seal, intending to restore a descendant of the Long house.

sentences.zh: 巡撫王廷相等破保，洸得還。

translations.literal: Grand coordinator Wang Tingxiang and others defeated Shabao, and Hao was able to return.
translations.idiomatic: Grand coordinator Wang Tingxiang and others defeated Shabao, and Cheng Hao was able to return.

sentences.zh: 保子普奴復連烏撒、水西苗攻剽畢節諸衛。

translations.literal: Shabao's son Punu again joined the Miao of Wusa and Shuixi in raiding the guards around Bijie.
translations.idiomatic: Shabao's son Punu again joined forces with the Wusa and Shuixi tribes in raiding the guards around Bijie.

sentences.zh: 帝命伍文定圖之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Wu Wending to devise a plan against them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Wu Wending to devise a plan to deal with them.

sentences.zh: 以朝議不合，召還。

translations.literal: Because court deliberation was divided, Yue was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Because court opinion was divided, he was recalled.

sentences.zh: 御史戴金因言：「芒部改流之議，諸司鹹執不可。

translations.literal: The censor Dai Jin thereupon said: "On the proposal to replace Mang rule with regular administration, all the offices firmly held that it could not be done.
