translations.idiomatic: Censor Dai Jin thereupon said: "On the proposal to replace Mang rule with regular administration, all the offices insisted that it could not be done.

sentences.zh: 軏徇洸邪說，違眾獨行，致疆場不靖。」

translations.literal: Yue followed Hao's perverse doctrine, defied the multitude and acted alone, and brought unrest to the frontier."
translations.idiomatic: Yue followed Cheng Hao's perverse proposal, defied consensus and acted on his own, and brought unrest to the frontier."

sentences.zh: 遂罷軏官。

translations.literal: Yue was thereupon dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Yue was thereupon dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 以兵部尚書李承勛薦，起故官，總督倉場。

translations.literal: On the recommendation of Minister of War Li Chengxun, he was reinstated in his former office and made grand coordinator of the granary depots.
translations.idiomatic: On the recommendation of Minister of War Li Chengxun, he was reinstated in his former post and appointed grand coordinator of the granary depots.

sentences.zh: 再遷南京戶部尚書。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to minister of revenue at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was again transferred to Minister of Revenue at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 御史龔湜劾軏老悖；

translations.literal: The censor Gong Shi impeached Yue as aged and perverse;
translations.idiomatic: Censor Gong Shi impeached Yue as aged and obstinate;

sentences.zh: 吏部言軏居官儉素，搢紳儀表。

translations.literal: the ministry of personnel said that in office Yue was frugal and plain and a model for the gentry and officials.
translations.idiomatic: the Ministry of Personnel replied that in office Yue was frugal and plain and a model for officials and gentry alike.

sentences.zh: 帝乃責湜妄言。

translations.literal: The emperor then rebuked Shi for reckless speech.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then rebuked Gong Shi for reckless accusations.

sentences.zh: 久之，就改兵部，參贊機務。

translations.literal: After a long while he was transferred on the spot to the ministry of war to assist in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was transferred on the spot to the Ministry of War to assist in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 詔舉將材，薦鄭卿、沈希儀等二十一人，皆擢用。

translations.literal: When an edict called for recommending military talent, he recommended Zheng Qing, Shen Xiyi, and twenty-one others in all, all of whom were promoted and employed.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict called for recommendations of military talent, he recommended Zheng Qing, Shen Xiyi, and twenty-one others in all, all of whom were promoted and employed.

sentences.zh: 居四年，以老乞罷。

translations.literal: After four years in office, on account of age he petitioned to be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: After four years in office, he petitioned to retire on account of age.

sentences.zh: 疏中言享年若干，帝以為非告君體，勒為民。

translations.literal: In his memorial he stated how many years he had lived; the emperor deemed this not the proper form of addressing one's ruler and ordered him reduced to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: In his memorial he stated how many years he had lived; the emperor deemed this an improper way to address one's sovereign and stripped him of office, reducing him to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 久之卒。

translations.literal: After a long while he died.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he died.

sentences.zh: 徐問，字用中，武進人。

translations.literal: Xu Wen, styled Yongzhong, was a native of Wujin.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Wen, styled Yongzhong, was a native of Wujin.

sentences.zh: 弘治十五年進士。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Hongzhi he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Hongzhi he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 授廣平推官。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating magistrate of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed investigating magistrate of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 遷刑部主事，歷兵部，出為登州知府。

translations.literal: He was transferred to principal secretary in the Ministry of Punishments, served in the Ministry of War, and went out as prefect of Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to a principal secretary in the Ministry of Punishments, served in the Ministry of War, and went out as prefect of Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 地濱海多盜，問盡捕之。

translations.literal: The region bordered the sea and had many bandits; Wen captured them all.
translations.idiomatic: The region bordered the sea and had many bandits; Wen captured them all.

sentences.zh: 調臨江。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Linjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Linjiang.

sentences.zh: 修築壞堤七十二。

translations.literal: He repaired seventy-two broken dikes.
translations.idiomatic: He repaired seventy-two broken dikes.

sentences.zh: 轉長蘆鹽運使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to salt transport commissioner of Changlu.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to salt transport commissioner of Changlu.

sentences.zh: 運司故利藪，自好者不樂居。

translations.literal: The transport office had long been a den of profit; men of integrity were unwilling to serve there.
translations.idiomatic: The transport office had long been a den of profit, and men of integrity were unwilling to serve there.

sentences.zh: 問曰：「吾欲清是官也。」

translations.literal: Wen said, "I wish to purify this office."
translations.idiomatic: Wen said, "I wish to purify this office."

sentences.zh: 終任不取一錢。

translations.literal: Throughout his term he did not take a single coin.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout his term he did not take a single coin.

sentences.zh: 累遷廣東左布政使。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Left Administration Commissioner of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to Left Administration Commissioner of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十一年以治行卓異，拜右副都御史，巡撫貴州。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Jiajing, on account of outstanding administrative conduct, he was appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Jiajing, on account of outstanding administrative merit, he was appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 獨山州賊蒙鉞弒父為亂。

translations.literal: At Dushan Prefecture the bandit Meng Yue murdered his father and rose in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: At Dushan Prefecture the bandit Meng Yue murdered his father and rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 問聞南丹、泗城欲助逆，檄廣西撫按伐其謀。

translations.literal: When Wen heard that Nandan and Sicheng intended to aid the rebels, he dispatched orders to the Guangxi grand coordinators and surveillance commissioners to thwart their plot.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen learned that Nandan and Sicheng intended to aid the rebels, he dispatched orders to the Guangxi grand coordinators and surveillance commissioners to thwart their plot.

sentences.zh: 又檄鉞弟釗復父仇，事平得承襲。

translations.literal: He also ordered Meng Yue's younger brother Zhao to avenge their father; when the affair was settled Zhao received the succession.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered Meng Yue's younger brother Zhao to avenge their father; when the affair was settled, Zhao received the succession.

sentences.zh: 鉞援絕。

translations.literal: Meng Yue's support was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Yue's support was cut off.

sentences.zh: 問督大兵分道入，誅之。

translations.literal: Wen supervised the main army entering by several routes and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Wen supervised the main army entering by several routes and executed him.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，賜金綺，召為兵部右侍郎。

translations.literal: When victory was reported, he was granted gold and brocade and summoned as Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: When victory was reported, he was granted gold and brocade and summoned as Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 疏陳武備八事。

translations.literal: In a memorial he set forth eight measures for military preparedness.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he set forth eight measures for military preparedness.

sentences.zh: 又言：「兩廣、雲、貴半土司，深山密菁，瑤、僮、羅、僰所窟穴。

translations.literal: He also said: "In the two Guang and Yunnan-Guizhou, half the territory is native chieftainships; in deep mountains and dense thickets lie the lairs of the Yao, Zhuang, Luo, and Bo.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "In the two Guang and in Yunnan-Guizhou, half the territory is under native chieftains; in deep mountains and dense thickets lie the lairs of the Yao, Zhuang, Luo, and Bo.

sentences.zh: 邊將喜功召釁，好為掃穴之舉。

translations.literal: Border generals, eager for merit, provoke incidents and love to mount campaigns to uproot whole nests.
translations.idiomatic: Border generals, eager for merit, provoke incidents and love to mount campaigns to uproot whole nests.

sentences.zh: 王師每入，巨憝潛蹤，所誅戮率無辜赤子。

translations.literal: Whenever the imperial army enters, the great villains slip away in hiding, and those killed are mostly innocent common people.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the imperial army enters, the great villains slip away in hiding, and those killed are mostly innocent common people.

sentences.zh: 興大兵，費厚餉，以易無辜命，非陛下好生意。

translations.literal: To raise a great army and spend heavy rations in exchange for innocent lives is not in keeping with Your Majesty's cherishing of life.
translations.idiomatic: To raise a great army and spend heavy rations in exchange for innocent lives is not in keeping with Your Majesty's cherishing of life.

sentences.zh: 宜敕邊臣布威信，嚴厄塞，謹哨探，使各安邊境，以絕禍萌。」

translations.literal: Border officials ought to be ordered to extend authority and trust, tighten strategic passes, keep careful watch at outposts, and let each side abide in its borders so the seeds of disaster are cut off at the start."
translations.idiomatic: Border officials ought to be ordered to extend authority and trust, tighten strategic passes, keep careful watch at outposts, and let each side abide within its borders so the seeds of disaster are cut off at the start."

sentences.zh: 帝深納其言。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply accepted his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deeply accepted his words.

sentences.zh: 尋引疾歸。

translations.literal: Soon he retired on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，召為南京禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was summoned as Vice Minister of Rites at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he was summoned as Vice Minister of Rites at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 久之，就遷戶部尚書。

translations.literal: After a long while he was transferred on the spot to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was transferred on the spot to Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 復引疾去，卒於家。

translations.literal: He again pleaded illness and left office, dying at home.
translations.idiomatic: He again pleaded illness and left office, and died at home.

sentences.zh: 問清節自勵。

translations.literal: Wen encouraged himself with incorrupt integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Wen held himself to incorrupt integrity.

sentences.zh: 居官四十年，敝廬蕭然，田不滿百畝。

translations.literal: In forty years of office his humble dwelling was bleakly empty and his fields did not amount to a hundred mu.
translations.idiomatic: In forty years of office his humble dwelling was bleakly empty, and his fields did not amount to a hundred mu.

sentences.zh: 好學不倦，粹然深造，為士類所宗。

translations.literal: He loved learning without weariness and attained pure, profound cultivation, and was revered by men of his kind.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning without weariness, attained pure and profound cultivation, and was revered by scholars.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，謚莊裕。

translations.literal: In the early Longqing reign he was posthumously enfeoffed with the title Zhuangyu.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Longqing reign he was posthumously granted the title Zhuangyu.

sentences.zh: 張邦奇，字常甫，鄞人。

translations.literal: Zhang Bangqi, styled Changfu, was a native of Yin county.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bangqi, styled Changfu, was a native of Yin county.

sentences.zh: 年十五作《易解》及《釋國語》。

translations.literal: At fifteen he composed "Explanations of the Changes" and "Exegesis of the Discourses of the States."
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he composed "Explanations of the Changes" and "Exegesis of the Discourses of the States."

sentences.zh: 登弘治末年進士，改庶吉士，授檢討。

translations.literal: In the final years of Hongzhi he passed the jinshi examination, was changed to Hanlin Bachelor, and appointed Erudite at the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the final years of Hongzhi he passed the jinshi examination, was made a Hanlin Bachelor, and appointed Erudite at the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 出為湖廣提學副使。

translations.literal: He went out as Vice Commissioner for Education in Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as Vice Commissioner for Education in Huguang.

sentences.zh: 下教曰：「學不孔、顏，行不曾、閔，雖文如雄、褒，吾且斥之。」

translations.literal: His instruction ran: "If one's learning is not that of Confucius and Yan Hui, and one's conduct not that of Zengzi and Min Ziqian—even if one's writing rivaled Yang Xiong and Liu Xiang, I shall reject such a one."
translations.idiomatic: His instruction ran: "If one's learning is not that of Confucius and Yan Hui, and one's conduct not that of Zengzi and Min Ziqian—even if one's writing rivaled Yang Xiong and Liu Xiang, I shall reject such a one."

sentences.zh: 在任三四年，諸生競勸。

translations.literal: In three or four years in office the students competed in moral effort.
translations.idiomatic: Within three or four years in office the students vied in moral cultivation.

sentences.zh: 時世宗方為興世子，獻皇遣就試。

translations.literal: At the time the future Jiajing Emperor was still heir to the Princedom of Xing; the Prince Xian sent him to take the examination.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the future Jiajing Emperor was still heir to the Princedom of Xing; Prince Xian sent him to take the examination.

sentences.zh: 乃特設兩案，己居北而使世子居南。

translations.literal: Bangqi specially set up two desks, placing himself on the north and the prince on the south.
translations.idiomatic: Bangqi specially set up two desks, placing himself on the north and the prince on the south.

sentences.zh: 文成，送入學。

translations.literal: When the compositions were finished, they were sent in to the school.
translations.idiomatic: When the compositions were finished, they were submitted to the school.

sentences.zh: 世宗由此知邦奇。

translations.literal: From this the prince came to know Bangqi.
translations.idiomatic: From this the prince came to know Bangqi.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，提學四川，以親孝乞歸。

translations.literal: In the early Jiajing reign he served as Commissioner for Education in Sichuan and begged leave to return on account of mourning for his parent.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Jiajing reign he served as Commissioner for Education in Sichuan and begged leave to return on account of mourning for his parent.

sentences.zh: 久之，桂萼掌銓，去留天下提學官，起邦奇福建。

translations.literal: After a long while Gui E took charge of the Board and reviewed all commissioners for education nationwide; Bangqi was recalled to Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: After some time Gui E took charge of the Board of Personnel and reviewed all commissioners for education nationwide; Bangqi was recalled to Fujian.

sentences.zh: 未幾，選外僚入坊局，改右庶子，遷南京祭酒。

translations.literal: Before long, outside officials were selected for the Eastern Palace and Secretariat; he was changed to Right Vice Director and transferred to Chancellor of the National University at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, outside officials were selected for the Eastern Palace and Secretariat; he was made Right Vice Director and transferred to Chancellor of the National University at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 以身為教，學規整肅。

translations.literal: He took his person as teaching, and the academic regulations were orderly and strict.
translations.idiomatic: He taught by his own example, and the academic regulations were orderly and strict.

sentences.zh: 就遷吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred on the spot to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred on the spot to Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 丁外艱歸。

translations.literal: On mourning for his father he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: On mourning for his father he returned home.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗奉太后謁天壽諸陵，語及擇相。

translations.literal: The emperor once accompanied the empress dowager on a visit to the Tianshou tombs and spoke of choosing a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once accompanied the empress dowager on a visit to the Tianshou tombs and spoke of choosing a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「先皇嘗言提學張邦奇器識，他日可為宰相，其人安在？」

translations.literal: The empress dowager said, "Your late father once said that the education commissioner Zhang Bangqi had ability and judgment and might one day serve as chief minister—where is that man now?"
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager said, "Your late father once said that the education commissioner Zhang Bangqi had ability and judgment and might one day serve as chief minister—where is that man now?"

sentences.zh: 帝憬然曰：「尚未用也。」

translations.literal: The emperor started and said, "He has not yet been employed."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor started and said, "He has not yet been employed."

sentences.zh: 服闋，即召為吏部右侍郎，掌部事。

translations.literal: When mourning was over he was at once summoned as Right Vice Minister of Personnel to manage the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning was over he was at once summoned as Right Vice Minister of Personnel to manage the ministry.

sentences.zh: 推轂善類，人不可幹以私。

translations.literal: He promoted worthy men and could not be swayed by private interests.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted worthy men and could not be swayed by private interests.

sentences.zh: 銓部升除，多受教政府，邦奇獨否，大學士李時銜之。

translations.literal: Appointments and dismissals in the Board often followed instructions from the chief ministers; Bangqi alone refused, and Grand Secretary Li Shi bore a grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Appointments and dismissals in the Board of Personnel often followed instructions from the chief ministers; Bangqi alone refused, and Grand Secretary Li Shi bore a grudge.

sentences.zh: 郭勛家人犯法，舁重賄請寬，邦奇不從。

translations.literal: When retainers of Guo Xun broke the law and offered heavy bribes seeking leniency, Bangqi would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: When retainers of Guo Xun broke the law and offered heavy bribes seeking leniency, Bangqi would not agree.

sentences.zh: 帝欲即授邦奇尚書，為兩人沮止。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to appoint Bangqi minister at once, but the two men obstructed and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to appoint Bangqi minister at once, but the two men obstructed and stopped it.

sentences.zh: 尋改掌翰林院事，充日講官，加太子賓客，改掌詹事府。

translations.literal: Soon he was reassigned to manage Hanlin Academy affairs, served as daily lecturer, was added as Tutor to the Heir Apparent, and transferred to manage the Household of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was reassigned to manage Hanlin Academy affairs, served as daily lecturer, was made Tutor to the Heir Apparent, and transferred to manage the Household of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 九載考績，晉禮部尚書。

translations.literal: At the nine-year performance review he was advanced to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: At the nine-year performance review he was advanced to Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 以母老欲便養，乃改南京吏部。

translations.literal: Because his mother was old and he wished to care for her nearby, he was changed to Minister of Personnel at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Because his mother was old and he wished to care for her nearby, he was transferred to Minister of Personnel at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 復改兵部，參贊機務。

translations.literal: He was again changed to the Ministry of War to assist in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was again transferred to the Ministry of War to assist in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝猶念邦奇，時與嚴嵩語及之。

translations.literal: The emperor still thought of Bangqi and from time to time spoke of him with Yan Song.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still thought of Bangqi and from time to time spoke of him with Yan Song.

sentences.zh: 嵩曰：「邦奇性至孝，母老，不樂北來。」

translations.literal: Yan Song said, "Bangqi is thoroughly filial by nature; his mother is old and he is unwilling to come north."
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song said, "Bangqi is thoroughly filial by nature; his mother is old and he is unwilling to come north."

sentences.zh: 帝信其言，遂不召。

translations.literal: The emperor believed his words and therefore did not summon him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor believed his words and therefore did not summon him.

sentences.zh: 二十三年卒，年六十一。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he died, aged sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he died, aged sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 贈太子太保，謚文定。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous title Wendi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous title Wendi.

sentences.zh: 邦奇之學以程、朱為宗。

translations.literal: Bangqi's learning took Cheng Hao and Zhu Xi as its standard.
translations.idiomatic: Bangqi's learning took Cheng Hao and Zhu Xi as its standard.

sentences.zh: 宗王守仁友善，而語每不合。

translations.literal: He was on friendly terms with Wang Shouren, yet their words often did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: He was on friendly terms with Wang Shouren, yet their words often did not agree.

sentences.zh: 躬修力踐，跬步必謹。

translations.literal: He cultivated himself in practice with every step careful.
translations.idiomatic: He cultivated himself in practice, careful at every step.

sentences.zh: 晝之所為，夕必書於冊。

translations.literal: What he did by day he necessarily wrote down in a book by evening.
translations.idiomatic: What he did by day he necessarily wrote down in a book by evening.

sentences.zh: 性篤孝，以養親故，屢起輒退。

translations.literal: By nature deeply filial, for the sake of supporting his parents he repeatedly accepted appointment only to retire.
translations.idiomatic: By nature deeply filial, for the sake of supporting his parents he repeatedly accepted appointment only to retire.

sentences.zh: 其母後邦奇卒，壽至百歲。

translations.literal: His mother survived him; she lived to a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: His mother survived him; she lived to a hundred.

sentences.zh: 邦奇事寡嫂如事母。

translations.literal: Bangqi served his widowed sister-in-law as he would his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Bangqi served his widowed sister-in-law as he would his mother.

sentences.zh: 所著《學庸傳》、《五經說》及文集，粹然一出於正。

translations.literal: His works "Commentary on the Great Learning and Doctrine of the Mean," "Treatises on the Five Classics," and collected writings are all purely within the orthodox tradition.
translations.idiomatic: His works "Commentary on the Great Learning and Doctrine of the Mean," "Treatises on the Five Classics," and his collected writings are all purely within the orthodox tradition.

sentences.zh: 族父時徹，少邦奇二十歲，受業於邦奇。

translations.literal: His clansman-uncle Shi Che was twenty years younger than Bangqi and received instruction from him.
translations.idiomatic: His clansman-uncle Shi Che was twenty years younger than Bangqi and studied under him.

sentences.zh: 仕至南京兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In office he rose to Minister of War at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In office he rose to Minister of War at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 有文名。

translations.literal: He had a literary reputation.
translations.idiomatic: He had a literary reputation.

sentences.zh: 韓邦奇，字汝節，朝邑人。

translations.literal: Han Bangqi, styled Rujie, was a native of Chaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: Han Bangqi, styled Rujie, was a native of Chaoyi.

sentences.zh: 父紹宗，福建副使。

translations.literal: His father Shaozong had been vice commissioner of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shaozong had served as vice commissioner of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 邦奇登正德三年進士，除吏部主事，進員外郎。

translations.literal: Bangqi passed the jinshi examination in the third year of Zhengde and was appointed principal secretary in the Ministry of Personnel, advancing to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: Bangqi passed the jinshi examination in the third year of Zhengde and was appointed principal secretary in the Ministry of Personnel, advancing to vice director.

sentences.zh: 六年冬，京師地震，上疏陳時政闕失。

translations.literal: In the winter of the sixth year, when the capital was shaken by an earthquake, he submitted a memorial setting forth the faults of current policy.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the sixth year, when the capital was shaken by an earthquake, he submitted a memorial setting forth the faults of current policy.

sentences.zh: 忤旨，不報。

translations.literal: He offended the imperial will and received no reply.
translations.idiomatic: He offended the imperial will and received no reply.

sentences.zh: 會給事中孫禎等劾臣僚不職者，並及邦奇。

translations.literal: At this time the supervising secretary Sun Zhen and others impeached officials for malfeasance and included Bangqi among them.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the supervising secretary Sun Zhen and others impeached officials for malfeasance and included Bangqi among them.

sentences.zh: 吏部已議留，帝竟以前疏故，黜為平陽通判。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel had already decided to retain him, but the emperor, on account of his earlier memorial after all, demoted him to vice magistrate of Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel had already decided to retain him, but the emperor, on account of his earlier memorial after all, demoted him to vice magistrate of Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 遷浙江僉事，轄杭、嚴二府。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice commissioner of Zhejiang, with jurisdiction over Hangzhou and Yanzhou prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice commissioner of Zhejiang, with jurisdiction over Hangzhou and Yanzhou prefectures.

sentences.zh: 宸濠令內豎假飯僧，聚千人於杭州天竺寺，邦奇立散遣之。

translations.literal: Zhu Chenhao sent a palace eunuch under the pretense of feeding monks to gather a thousand men at Tianzhu Temple in Hangzhou; Bangqi immediately dispersed and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Chenhao sent a palace eunuch under the pretense of feeding monks to gather a thousand men at Tianzhu Temple in Hangzhou; Bangqi immediately dispersed and sent them away.

sentences.zh: 其儀賓托進貢假道衢州，邦奇詰之曰：「入貢當沿江下，奚自假道？

translations.literal: When a ritual guest of the prince sought passage through Quzhou on the pretext of presenting tribute, Bangqi interrogated him and said, "Tribute should proceed down the Yangzi River—why take this roundabout route?
translations.idiomatic: When a ritual guest of the prince sought passage through Quzhou on the pretext of presenting tribute, Bangqi interrogated him and said, "Tribute should proceed down the Yangzi River—why take this roundabout route?

sentences.zh: 歸語王，韓僉事不可誑也。」

translations.literal: Return and tell the prince: Vice Commissioner Han cannot be deceived."
translations.idiomatic: Return and tell the prince: Vice Commissioner Han cannot be deceived."

sentences.zh: 時中官在浙者凡四人，王堂為鎮守，晁進督織造，崔泬主市舶，張玉管營造。

translations.literal: At the time there were four eunuchs in Zhejiang: Wang Tang as military commissioner, Chao Jin supervising weaving, Cui Jiong in charge of the customs bureau, and Zhang Yu managing construction.
translations.idiomatic: At the time there were four eunuchs in Zhejiang: Wang Tang as military commissioner, Chao Jin supervising weaving, Cui Jiong in charge of the customs bureau, and Zhang Yu managing construction.

sentences.zh: 爪牙四出，民不聊生。

translations.literal: Their claws reached everywhere and the people had no livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: Their agents reached everywhere and the people had no livelihood.

sentences.zh: 邦奇疏請禁止，又數裁抑堂。

translations.literal: Bangqi memorialized requesting a ban, and repeatedly curbed Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Bangqi memorialized requesting a ban, and repeatedly curbed Tang.

sentences.zh: 邦奇閔中官采富陽茶魚為民害，作歌哀之。

translations.literal: Bangqi pitied the people over the harm done by eunuchs collecting tea and fish at Fuyang and composed a lament.
translations.idiomatic: Bangqi pitied the people over the harm done by eunuchs collecting tea and fish at Fuyang and composed a lament.

sentences.zh: 堂遂奏邦奇沮格上供，作歌怨謗。

translations.literal: Tang then memorialized that Bangqi obstructed tribute to the court and composed a song of resentment and slander.
translations.idiomatic: Tang then memorialized that Bangqi obstructed tribute to the court and composed a song of resentment and slander.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，逮至京，下詔獄。

translations.literal: The emperor was enraged, had him arrested and brought to the capital, and placed him in the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged, had him arrested and brought to the capital, and placed him in the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 廷臣論救，皆不聽，斥為民。

translations.literal: Court officials pleaded for mercy but none was heeded; he was dismissed as a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials pleaded for mercy but none was heeded; he was dismissed as a commoner.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，起山東參議。

translations.literal: In the early Jiajing reign he was recalled as administration commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Jiajing reign he was recalled as administration commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 乞休去。

translations.literal: He begged leave to retire and departed.
translations.idiomatic: He requested retirement and left office.

sentences.zh: 尋用薦，以故官蒞山西。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter, on recommendation, he came to Shanxi in his former rank.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, on recommendation, he took up his former post in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 再乞休去。

translations.literal: Again he begged leave to retire and departed.
translations.idiomatic: He again requested retirement and left office.

sentences.zh: 起四川提學副使，入為春坊右庶子。

translations.literal: He was recalled as vice commissioner of education for Sichuan, then entered the capital as right assistant in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as vice education intendant of Sichuan, then entered the capital as right assistant in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 七年偕同官方鵬主應天鄉試，坐試錄謬誤，謫南京太仆丞。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, together with his colleague Fang Peng he presided over the provincial examination of Yingtian; for errors in the examination record he was demoted to vice director of the Nanjing Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, together with his colleague Fang Peng he presided over the Yingtian provincial examination; for errors in the examination record he was demoted to vice director of the Nanjing Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 復乞歸。

translations.literal: Again he begged to return home.
translations.idiomatic: He again asked to return home.

sentences.zh: 起山東副使，遷大理丞，進少卿，以右僉都御史巡撫宣府。

translations.literal: Recalled as vice commissioner of Shandong, he was transferred to assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review, advanced to vice director, and as right vice censor-in-chief supervised Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as vice commissioner of Shandong, he was transferred to assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review, promoted to vice director, and appointed right vice censor-in-chief to supervise Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 入佐院事，進右副都御史，巡撫遼東。

translations.literal: He entered to assist in censorate affairs, was advanced to right vice censor-in-chief, and supervised Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital to assist in censorate affairs, was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief, and supervised Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 時遼陽兵變，侍郎黃宗明言邦奇素有威望，請假以便宜，速往定亂。

translations.literal: At the time the troops at Liaoyang mutinied; Vice Minister Huang Zongming said Bangqi had long possessed prestige and requested that discretionary authority be granted him to go quickly and settle the disorder.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the troops at Liaoyang mutinied; Vice Minister Huang Zongming said Bangqi had long enjoyed great prestige and asked that he be granted discretionary authority to go quickly and put down the disturbance.

sentences.zh: 帝方事姑息，不從，命與山西巡撫任洛換官。

translations.literal: The emperor was then practicing indulgence and did not agree; he ordered Bangqi and Ren Luo, grand coordinator of Shanxi, to exchange posts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then inclined to leniency and would not agree; he ordered Bangqi and Ren Luo, grand coordinator of Shanxi, to exchange posts.

sentences.zh: 至山西，為政嚴肅，有司供具悉不納，間日出俸米易肉一斤。

translations.literal: Arriving in Shanxi, his administration was stern; he accepted none of the provisions offered by officials, and from time to time traded a portion of his salary grain for one jin of meat.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Shanxi, he governed with strict severity, refused all provisions offered by subordinate officials, and from time to time exchanged part of his salary grain for a pound of meat.

sentences.zh: 居四年，引疾歸。

translations.literal: After four years in office, he cited illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: After four years in office, he cited illness and retired.

sentences.zh: 中外交薦，以故官起督河道。

translations.literal: Recommended within and without the court, he was recalled in his former rank to supervise the waterways.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended at court and beyond, he was recalled to his former rank to supervise the waterways.

sentences.zh: 遷刑部右侍郎，改吏部。

translations.literal: He was transferred to right vice minister of Justice, then shifted to Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to right vice minister of Justice, then to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 拜南京右都御史，進兵部尚書，參贊機務。

translations.literal: He received appointment as right censor-in-chief at Nanjing, was advanced to minister of War, and assisted in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed right censor-in-chief at Nanjing, promoted to minister of War, and assisted in state affairs.

sentences.zh: 致仕歸。

translations.literal: He retired from office and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He retired and returned home.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，陜西地大震，邦奇隕焉。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year a great earthquake struck Shaanxi, and Bangqi perished in it.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year a great earthquake struck Shaanxi, and Bangqi was killed.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少保，謚恭簡。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous name Gongjian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous name Gongjian ("Respectful and Simple").

sentences.zh: 邦奇性嗜學。

translations.literal: By nature Bangqi loved learning.
translations.idiomatic: Bangqi was by nature devoted to learning.

sentences.zh: 自諸經、子、史及天文、地理、樂律、術數、兵法之書，無不通究。

translations.literal: From the Classics, masters, and histories to books on astronomy, geography, music, calculation, and warfare—there was none he did not thoroughly investigate.
translations.idiomatic: From the Classics, masters, and histories to works on astronomy, geography, music, calendrical science, divination, and military strategy, there was virtually no field he had not mastered.

sentences.zh: 著述甚富。

translations.literal: His writings were very abundant.
translations.idiomatic: His writings were extensive.

sentences.zh: 所撰《誌樂》，尤為世所稱。

translations.literal: His work Records of Music was especially praised by the world.
translations.idiomatic: His treatise Records of Music was especially acclaimed.

sentences.zh: 弟邦靖，字汝度。

translations.literal: His younger brother Bangjing, styled Rudu.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Bangjing, styled Rudu.

sentences.zh: 年十四舉於鄉。

translations.literal: At fourteen he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he passed the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 與邦奇同登進士，授工部主事。

translations.literal: Together with Bangqi he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed principal secretary in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He and Bangqi passed the jinshi examination together; he was appointed principal secretary in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 榷木浙江，額不充，被劾，以守官廉得免。

translations.literal: Levying timber in Zhejiang, the quota was not met and he was impeached; because he had kept his office incorrupt he was excused.
translations.idiomatic: While collecting timber levies in Zhejiang he failed to meet the quota and was impeached, but was excused on grounds of incorrupt service.

sentences.zh: 進員外郎。

translations.literal: He was advanced to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director.

sentences.zh: 乾清宮災，指斥時政甚切。

translations.literal: When the Qianqing Palace caught fire, he criticized current policy with great severity.
translations.idiomatic: After the Qianqing Palace burned, he criticized current policy in the sharpest terms.

sentences.zh: 武宗大怒，下之詔獄。

translations.literal: Emperor Wuzong was greatly enraged and had him sent to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wuzong was furious and had him thrown into the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 給事中李鐸等以為言，乃奪職為民。

translations.literal: The supervising secretaries Li Duo and others spoke on his behalf, whereupon he was only stripped of office and made a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretaries Li Duo and others pleaded for him, and he was merely stripped of office and dismissed to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，起山西左參議，分守大同。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, he was recalled as left administration commissioner of Shanxi, with separate charge of Datong.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong acceded, he was recalled as left administration commissioner of Shanxi to defend Datong.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，人相食，奏請發帑，不許。

translations.literal: In a year of famine people ate one another; he memorialized requesting disbursement from the treasury, but permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: In a famine year people resorted to cannibalism; he memorialized asking that funds be released from the treasury, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 復抗疏千余言，不報。

translations.literal: Again he submitted a defiant memorial of more than a thousand characters and received no reply.
translations.idiomatic: He again submitted a forthright memorial of more than a thousand characters and received no response.

sentences.zh: 乞歸，不待命輒行。

translations.literal: He begged to return home and, without awaiting orders, left at once.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to retire and left without waiting for imperial approval.

sentences.zh: 軍民遮道泣留。

translations.literal: Soldiers and civilians blocked the road, weeping to detain him.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers and civilians barred the road, weeping as they tried to keep him from leaving.

sentences.zh: 抵家病卒，年三十六。

translations.literal: Reaching home, he died of illness at the age of thirty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He reached home and died of illness at thirty-six.

sentences.zh: 未幾，邦奇亦以參議蒞大同。

translations.literal: Before long Bangqi also came to Datong as administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Bangqi likewise arrived at Datong as administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 父老因邦靖故，前迎，皆泣下。

translations.literal: The elders, because of Bangjing, went forward to welcome him, all weeping.
translations.idiomatic: The local elders, remembering Bangjing, came forward to greet him, all in tears.

sentences.zh: 邦奇亦泣。

translations.literal: Bangqi wept as well.
translations.idiomatic: Bangqi wept as well.

sentences.zh: 邦奇嘗廬居，病歲餘不能起。

translations.literal: Bangqi once lived in a mourning hut; for more than a year he was ill and could not rise.
translations.idiomatic: Bangqi once lived in a mourning hut and was bedridden for more than a year.

sentences.zh: 邦靖藥必分嘗，食飲皆手進。

translations.literal: Bangjing always tasted medicine before giving it, and brought food and drink by hand.
translations.idiomatic: Bangjing always tasted his brother's medicine first and personally served his food and drink.

sentences.zh: 後邦靖病亟，邦奇日夜持弟泣，不解衣者三月。

translations.literal: Later, when Bangjing was gravely ill, Bangqi day and night held his younger brother weeping, for three months not removing his clothes.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Bangjing fell gravely ill, Bangqi held his brother day and night, weeping; for three months he never undressed.

sentences.zh: 及歿，衰绖蔬食，終喪弗懈。

translations.literal: When he died, Bangqi wore mourning garb and ate plain food, never slackening through the full mourning period.
translations.idiomatic: After his death Bangqi wore hemp mourning and ate plain fare, never relaxing observance through the full mourning period.

sentences.zh: 鄉人為立「孝弟碑」。

translations.literal: The villagers erected for him a stele entitled "Filial Piety and Brotherly Love."
translations.idiomatic: The villagers erected for him a stele entitled "Filial Piety and Brotherly Affection."

sentences.zh: 周金，字子庚，武進人。

translations.literal: Zhou Jin, styled Zigeng, was a native of Wujin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Jin, styled Zigeng, was a native of Wujin.

sentences.zh: 正德三年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi of the third year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the third year of Zhengde.

sentences.zh: 授工科給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed supervising secretary of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed supervising secretary in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 累遷戶科都給事中。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to chief supervising secretary of the Revenue Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to chief supervising secretary of the Revenue Bureau.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「京糧歲入三百五萬，而食者乃四百三萬，當痛為澄汰。

translations.literal: In a memorial he said: "Annual intake of grain for the capital is 3.5 million, yet those fed number 4.3 million—this must be ruthlessly clarified and purged.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he wrote: "Annual grain intake for the capital is 3.5 million piculs, yet those receiving rations number 4.3 million—the rolls must be ruthlessly purged.

sentences.zh: 中官迎佛及監織造者濫乞引鹽，暴橫道路，當罷。

translations.literal: Palace eunuchs who welcome the Buddha and those who supervise weaving recklessly beg salt vouchers and are violent and overbearing on the roads—they should be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Palace eunuchs escorting Buddhist images and supervisors of imperial weaving who indiscriminately seek salt vouchers and swagger violently along the roads should be suppressed.

sentences.zh: 都督馬昂納有妊女弟，當誅昂而還其女。」

translations.literal: The commander Ma Ang accepted as wife his younger sister who was pregnant—Ang should be put to death and the woman returned."
translations.idiomatic: Commander Ma Ang took in his pregnant younger sister as a concubine—Ang should be executed and the woman sent home."

sentences.zh: 朝議用兵土魯番，復哈密。

translations.literal: The court debated raising troops against Turfan to recover Hami.
translations.idiomatic: The court debated military action against Turfan to recover Hami.

sentences.zh: 金言西邊虛憊，而土魯番險遠，且青海之寇窺伺西寧，不宜計哈密。

translations.literal: Jin said the western border was empty and exhausted, Turfan was perilous and remote, and moreover bandits from Qinghai were watching Xining—it was inappropriate to fix plans on Hami.
translations.idiomatic: Jin argued that the western frontier was drained and weak, Turfan was dangerous and remote, and Qinghai raiders were eyeing Xining—Hami should not be the focus of strategy.

sentences.zh: 已，卒從金議。

translations.literal: In the end the court followed Jin's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the court adopted Jin's view.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖元年由太仆寺少卿遷都察院右僉都御史，巡撫延綏。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiajing he moved from vice director of the Court of the Imperial Stud to right vice censor-in-chief of the Censorate, supervising Yan-sui.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiajing he was transferred from vice director of the Court of the Imperial Stud to right vice censor-in-chief, with authority over Yan-sui.

sentences.zh: 邊人貧甚。

translations.literal: The border people were extremely poor.
translations.idiomatic: The border population was desperately poor.

sentences.zh: 金為招商聚粟，廣屯積芻，以時給其食。

translations.literal: Jin invited merchants to gather grain, broadly opened farming colonies and stored fodder, and timely provided their food.
translations.idiomatic: Jin encouraged merchants to bring in grain, expanded garrison farming and fodder stores, and saw that provisions were distributed on schedule.

sentences.zh: 改撫宣府，進右副都御史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to supervise Xuanfu and advanced to right vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned to supervise Xuanfu and promoted to right vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 大同叛卒殺張文錦，邊鎮兵皆驕。

translations.literal: Mutinous soldiers at Datong killed Zhang Wenjin, and troops at all border garrisons grew arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: Mutinous troops at Datong killed Zhang Wenjin, and soldiers at every border garrison grew unruly.

sentences.zh: 宣府總督侍郎馮清苛刻。

translations.literal: Feng Qing, vice minister and grand coordinator of Xuanfu, was harsh and exacting.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Qing, vice minister and grand coordinator of Xuanfu, was harsh and overbearing.

sentences.zh: 諸軍請糧不從，且欲鞭之，眾轟然圍清府署。

translations.literal: The troops requested grain and were refused; he even wished to flog them, and the crowd with a roar surrounded Qing's official residence.
translations.idiomatic: When the troops asked for rations he refused, and even threatened to flog them; with a roar the men surrounded Feng Qing's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 金方病，出坐院門，召諸軍官數之曰：「是若輩剝削之過！」

translations.literal: Jin was then ill; he came out and sat at the gate of the yamen, summoned the military officers, and rebuked them, saying: "This is your fault for extortion!"
translations.idiomatic: Jin was ill at the time; he came out and sat at the yamen gate, summoned the officers, and rebuked them: "This is your fault for extorting the men!"

sentences.zh: 欲痛鞭之。

translations.literal: He wished to flog them severely.
translations.idiomatic: He threatened to flog them severely.

sentences.zh: 軍士氣稍平，擁而前請曰：「總制不恤我耳！」

translations.literal: The soldiers' temper calmed somewhat; pressing forward they pleaded: "The grand coordinator simply does not care for us!"
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers' anger eased somewhat; pressing forward they cried: "The grand coordinator does not care for us at all!"

sentences.zh: 金從容諭以利害，眾乃散解去，得無變。

translations.literal: Jin calmly instructed them on advantage and harm; the crowd then dispersed and withdrew, and there was no disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: Jin calmly explained the consequences; the men then dispersed, and no disturbance arose.

sentences.zh: 改撫保定。

translations.literal: He was transferred to supervise Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned to supervise Baoding.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史李新芳疑廣平知縣謀己，欲抶之。

translations.literal: The touring investigating censor Li Xinfang suspected the magistrate of Guangping of plotting against him and wished to beat him with the cudgel.
translations.idiomatic: Touring investigating censor Li Xinfang suspected the magistrate of Guangping of plotting against him and wished to have him beaten.

sentences.zh: 知府為之解，並欲執知府，發兵二千捕之。

translations.literal: The prefect sought to explain on his behalf; Li also wished to seize the prefect, and dispatched two thousand troops to arrest him.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect intervened on the magistrate's behalf; Li then tried to seize the prefect as well and sent two thousand troops to capture him.

sentences.zh: 知府及佐貳皆走，一城盡空。

translations.literal: The prefect and his assistants all fled, and the whole city was emptied.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect and his deputies all fled, and the city was left deserted.

sentences.zh: 金發其罪狀，而都御史王廷相庇新芳，與相爭。

translations.literal: Jin exposed his crimes, but the censor-in-chief Wang Tingxiang sheltered Xinfang, and they contended with each other.
translations.idiomatic: Jin exposed Li's misconduct, but censor-in-chief Wang Tingxiang shielded Xinfang, and the two clashed.

sentences.zh: 帝卒下新芳刑部，黜官。

translations.literal: The emperor finally sent Xinfang to the Ministry of Justice and dismissed him from office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor eventually handed Xinfang over to the Ministry of Justice and removed him from office.

sentences.zh: 金遷兵部右侍郎。

translations.literal: Jin was transferred to right vice minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was transferred to right vice minister of War.

sentences.zh: 未幾，進右都御史，總督漕運，巡撫鳳陽諸府。

translations.literal: Before long he was advanced to right censor-in-chief, grand coordinator of the grain transport, supervising the prefectures around Fengyang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to right censor-in-chief, placed in charge of the Grand Canal transport, and given supervision over the Fengyang region.

sentences.zh: 久之，擢南京刑部尚書，就轉戶部。

translations.literal: After a long time he was elevated to minister of Justice at Nanjing, then directly transferred to Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: After some years he was promoted to minister of Justice at Nanjing, then moved directly to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 二十四年致仕歸，歲餘卒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he retired and returned home; a little more than a year later he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he retired; a little over a year later he died.

sentences.zh: 贈太子太保，謚襄敏。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous name Xiangmin.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous name Xiangmin.

sentences.zh: 吳嶽，字汝喬，汶上人。

translations.literal: Wu Yue, styled Rujiao, was a native of Wenshang.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yue, styled Rujiao, was a native of Wenshang.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十一年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi of the eleventh year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the eleventh year of Jiajing.

sentences.zh: 授戶部主事，歷郎中。

translations.literal: He was appointed principal secretary in the Ministry of Revenue and served successively as director.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed principal secretary in the Ministry of Revenue and rose to serve as director.

sentences.zh: 督餉宣府，吏進羨金數千，拒之。

translations.literal: Supervising provisions at Xuanfu, clerks offered several thousand in supplementary silver; he refused it.
translations.idiomatic: While supervising grain supplies at Xuanfu, clerks offered him several thousand taels in "supplementary" silver; he refused.

sentences.zh: 出知廬州府。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as prefect of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 稅課歲萬金，例輸府，嶽以代郵傳費。

translations.literal: Tax levies amounted to ten thousand taels yearly, which by rule were paid to the prefectural office; Yue used them in place of courier expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Annual tax receipts came to ten thousand taels, which by custom went to the prefectural treasury; Yue applied them to courier expenses instead.

sentences.zh: 西山薪故供官爨，嶽弛以利民。

translations.literal: Fuel from West Mountain had formerly supplied official kitchens; Yue relaxed this to benefit the people.
translations.idiomatic: Firewood from West Mountain had formerly been reserved for official use; Yue lifted the restriction to ease the burden on the people.

sentences.zh: 以憂去。

translations.literal: He left office on account of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 服除，改保定，治如廬州。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was transferred to Baoding and governed as he had at Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning ended he was assigned to Baoding and governed there as he had at Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 歷山西副使、浙江參政、湖廣按察使、山西右布政使，並以清靜得民。

translations.literal: He served successively as vice commissioner of Shanxi, administration commissioner of Zhejiang, surveillance commissioner of Huguang, and right administration commissioner of Shanxi, and in each post won the people through his quiet integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice commissioner of Shanxi, administration commissioner of Zhejiang, surveillance commissioner of Huguang, and right administration commissioner of Shanxi, winning popular esteem everywhere through quiet, upright government.

sentences.zh: 遷右僉都御史，巡撫保定六府。

translations.literal: He was transferred to right vice censor-in-chief, supervising the six prefectures of Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief and given supervision over the six Baoding prefectures.

sentences.zh: 奏裁征發冗費十六七，民力遂寬。

translations.literal: He memorialized cutting redundant levies by six or seven tenths, and the people's burdens were thereby eased.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to cut redundant levies by six or seven tenths, greatly easing the burden on the people.

sentences.zh: 甫浹歲，引疾去。

translations.literal: Barely a full year had passed when he cited illness and left.
translations.idiomatic: After barely a year he cited illness and retired.

sentences.zh: 久之，以貴州巡撫征。

translations.literal: After a long time he was summoned as grand coordinator of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After some years he was recalled to serve as grand coordinator of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 尋進左副都御史，協理院事。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to left vice censor-in-chief and assisted in managing censorate affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to left vice censor-in-chief and assisted in managing the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 隆慶元年，歷吏部左、右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longqing he served successively as left and right vice minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longqing he served successively as left and right vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 京察竣，給事中胡應嘉有所申救。

translations.literal: When the capital inspection was concluded, the supervising secretary Hu Yingjia made representations to save someone.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital civil inspection, supervising secretary Hu Yingjia intervened on behalf of an official marked for dismissal.

sentences.zh: 嶽詣內閣抗聲曰：「科臣敢留考察罷黜官，有故事乎？」

translations.literal: Yue went to the Grand Secretariat and in a loud voice said: "Does a supervising censor dare retain an official dismissed in the inspection—is there precedent for this?"
translations.idiomatic: Yue went to the Grand Secretariat and demanded in a loud voice: "When has a supervising censor ever kept in office someone the inspection marked for dismissal—is there any precedent for that?"

sentences.zh: 應嘉遂得譴。

translations.literal: Yingjia was thereupon punished.
translations.idiomatic: Yingjia was thereupon punished.

sentences.zh: 遷南京禮部尚書，就改吏部。

translations.literal: He was transferred to minister of Rites at Nanjing, then directly shifted to Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to minister of Rites at Nanjing, then moved directly to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 抑浮薄，杜僥幸，南都縉紳憚之。

translations.literal: He checked frivolity and blocked opportunism; the gentry and officials of the southern capital feared him.
translations.idiomatic: He curbed frivolous conduct and shut off opportunism, and the officials of the southern capital stood in awe of him.

sentences.zh: 上疏陳六事，帝頗納其言。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial setting forth six matters; the emperor largely adopted his words.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on six policy points, and the emperor largely accepted his recommendations.

sentences.zh: 尋改兵部，參贊機務。

translations.literal: Soon he was shifted to the Ministry of War to assist in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was moved to the Ministry of War to assist in state affairs.

sentences.zh: 未上，給由過家，病卒。

translations.literal: Before he had taken up the post, he was granted leave to pass through his home and died of illness on the way.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could assume the post, he was granted leave to visit home and died of illness en route.

sentences.zh: 詔贈太子太保，謚介肅。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously enfeoffed him as grand mentor to the heir apparent and gave him the posthumous name Jiesu.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Mentor to the Heir Apparent and gave him the posthumous name Jiesu (Incorruptible and Solemn).

sentences.zh: 嶽清望冠一時，禔躬嚴整。

translations.literal: Yue's pure reputation stood foremost in his age, and his personal conduct was stern and orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Yue's reputation for integrity stood foremost in his age, and his personal conduct was stern and orderly.

sentences.zh: 尚書馬森言平生見廉節士二人，嶽與譚大初耳。

translations.literal: The minister Ma Sen said that in his life he had seen only two men of incorruptible integrity—Yue and Tan Dachu.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister Ma Sen said that in his life he had seen only two men of incorruptible integrity—Yue and Tan Dachu.

sentences.zh: 嶽知廬州時，王廷守蘇州，以公事遇京口。

translations.literal: When Yue was prefect of Luzhou, Wang Ting was defending Suzhou; they met at Jingkou on official business.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue was prefect of Luzhou, Wang Ting was defending Suzhou; they met at Jingkou on official business.

sentences.zh: 嶽召為金山遊，攜酒一缶，肉一斤，菜數束。

translations.literal: Yue invited him on an outing to Jinshan, bringing one jar of wine, a pound of meat, and several bundles of vegetables.
translations.idiomatic: Yue invited him on an outing to Jinshan, bringing one jar of wine, a pound of meat, and several bundles of vegetables.

sentences.zh: 廷笑曰：「止是乎？」

translations.literal: Ting laughed and said, "Is this all?
translations.idiomatic: Ting laughed and said, "Is this all?

sentences.zh: 嶽亦笑曰：「足供我兩人食矣。」

translations.literal: Yue also laughed and said, "It is enough to feed the two of us.
translations.idiomatic: Yue also laughed and said, "It is enough to feed the two of us.

sentences.zh: 歡竟日而還。

translations.literal: They rejoiced the whole day and returned.
translations.idiomatic: They enjoyed themselves the whole day and returned.

sentences.zh: 去廬日，假一蓋禦雨，至即命還之。

translations.literal: On the day he left Luzhou he borrowed an umbrella against rain and, upon arrival, immediately ordered it returned.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he left Luzhou he borrowed an umbrella against the rain and, upon arrival, immediately ordered it returned.

sentences.zh: 譚大初，字宗元，始興人。

translations.literal: Tan Dachu, styled Zongyuan, was a man of Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Dachu, styled Zongyuan, was a native of Shixing.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十七年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the seventeenth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Jiajing 17.

sentences.zh: 授工部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed a principal secretary in the ministry of works.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a principal secretary in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 憂歸。

translations.literal: He returned home in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 起補戶部，改戶科給事中。

translations.literal: He was recalled to the ministry of revenue and transferred to supervising secretary in the bureau of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the Ministry of Revenue and transferred to supervising secretary in the Bureau of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 數論事。

translations.literal: He repeatedly remonstrated on state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly remonstrated on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 歷兵科左給事中，出為江西副使。

translations.literal: He served as left supervising secretary in the bureau of military affairs, then went out as vice commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He served as left supervising secretary in the Bureau of Military Affairs, then went out as vice commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 清軍，多所釋。

translations.literal: While inspecting troops he released many men.
translations.idiomatic: While inspecting troops he released many men.

sentences.zh: 御史孫慎以失額為疑，大初曰：「失額罪小，殃民罪大。」

translations.literal: The censor Sun Shen suspected him of shortfall in quotas; Dachu said, "A shortfall is a small offense; harming the people is a great one.
translations.idiomatic: The censor Sun Shen suspected him of shortfall in quotas; Dachu said, "A shortfall is a small offense; harming the people is a great one.

sentences.zh: 嚴嵩親黨奪民田，治之不少貸。

translations.literal: When kinsmen of Yan Song seized the people's fields, he punished them without leniency.
translations.idiomatic: When kinsmen of Yan Song seized the people's fields, he punished them without leniency.

sentences.zh: 遷廣西右參政，投劾歸。

translations.literal: He was transferred to right assistant administration commissioner of Guangxi and submitted an impeachment of himself to retire.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Right Assistant Administration Commissioner of Guangxi and submitted an impeachment of himself to retire.

sentences.zh: 久之，起故官河南。

translations.literal: After a long while he was recalled to his former office in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he was recalled to his former office in Henan.

sentences.zh: 未上，擢南京右通政。

translations.literal: Before he took up the post he was promoted to right vice commissioner of transmissions at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Before he took up the post he was promoted to Right Vice Commissioner of Transmissions at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 俄遷應天府尹。

translations.literal: Shortly he was transferred to be prefect of Yingtian.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly he was transferred to be prefect of Yingtian.

sentences.zh: 將赴南都，而穆宗即位，乞以參政致仕，不許。

translations.literal: As he was about to go to the southern capital, the Muzong Emperor ascended the throne; he asked to retire with the rank of administration commissioner, but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to go to the southern capital, Emperor Muzong ascended the throne; he asked to retire with the rank of administration commissioner, but was not permitted.

sentences.zh: 隆慶元年召拜工部右侍郎，尋遷戶部左侍郎，督倉場。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longqing he was summoned as right vice minister of works, then soon transferred to left vice minister of revenue with charge of the granary depots.
translations.idiomatic: In Longqing 1 he was summoned as Right Vice Minister of Works, then soon transferred to Left Vice Minister of Revenue with charge of the granary depots.

sentences.zh: 海瑞為僉都御史，大初力薦瑞。

translations.literal: When Hai Rui was made censor-in-chief, Dachu strongly recommended Rui.
translations.idiomatic: When Hai Rui was made censor-in-chief, Dachu strongly recommended him.

sentences.zh: 已而屢疏乞休，不允。

translations.literal: Later he repeatedly memorialized to retire, but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Later he repeatedly memorialized to retire, but was not permitted.

sentences.zh: 拜南京戶部尚書，引疾去。

translations.literal: He was appointed minister of revenue at Nanjing and retired citing illness.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Minister of Revenue at Nanjing and retired citing illness.

sentences.zh: 家居，田不及百畝。

translations.literal: At home his fields amounted to less than a hundred mu.
translations.idiomatic: At home his fields amounted to less than a hundred mu.

sentences.zh: 卒年七十五。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 謚莊懿。

translations.literal: He was given the posthumous name Zhuangyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous name Zhuangyi (Solemn and Kind).

sentences.zh: 贊曰：當正、嘉之際，士大夫刓方為圓，貶其素履，羔羊素絲之節浸以微矣。

translations.literal: The commentator says: In the Zhengde and Jiajing era, scholar-officials planed the square into the round, belittled their plain conduct, and the integrity of the lamb and the white silk grew ever faint.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: In the Zhengde and Jiajing era, scholar-officials planed the square into the round, belittled their plain conduct, and the integrity symbolized by the lamb and the white silk grew ever faint.

sentences.zh: 陶琰諸人清操峻特，卓然可風。

translations.literal: Tao Yan and his fellows were stern and exceptional in pure conduct, standing forth as models to be emulated.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Yan and his fellows were stern and exceptional in pure conduct, standing forth as models to be emulated.

sentences.zh: 南都列卿，後先相望，不其賢乎。

translations.literal: The chief ministers of the southern capital followed one upon another—were they not worthy men?
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers of the southern capital followed one upon another—were they not worthy men?

sentences.zh: 琰之督漕，充嗣之守禦，良永之遏錢寧，周金之弭亂卒，所豎立甚偉。

translations.literal: Yan's direction of grain transport, Chongsi's defense, Liangyong's curbing of Qian Ning, and Jin's quelling of mutinous troops—the achievements they raised up were very great.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's direction of grain transport, Chongsi's defense, Liangyong's curbing of Qian Ning, and Jin's quelling of mutinous troops—the achievements they raised up were very great.

sentences.zh: 至琰子之直節，廷弼、邦靖之篤行，尤無忝其父兄雲。

translations.literal: As for the upright integrity of Yan's son, and the devoted conduct of Tingbi and Bangjing, they especially did not disgrace their fathers and elder brothers.
translations.idiomatic: As for the upright integrity of Yan's son, and the devoted conduct of Tingbi and Bangjing, they especially did not disgrace their fathers and elder brothers.
